### 1. Vitest 5.0 Pre-Release Planning — Breaking Mock Defaults and Multi-Runtime Support

Vitest 5.0 (planned Q3 2026, ~2 months from the February 2026 discussion start) introduces two category-defining breaking changes that directly affect how test suites are structured across pyramid levels.

**Breaking change 1: `clearMocks`, `mockReset`, or `restoreMocks` enabled by default.** Currently every Vitest project must manually configure mock cleanup, leading to silent state leakage between test cases at the unit level. Vitest 5.0 will default to one of these options (community vote ongoing), eliminating a leading cause of order-dependent unit test flakiness.

**Breaking change 2: Multi-runtime project configuration.** Vitest 5.0 allows a single `vitest.config.ts` to dispatch test projects to different runtimes — Node.js, Deno, and Bun — in a single run. This is pyramid-significant: library authors can now validate that utility functions (unit level) behave identically across all three runtimes without maintaining separate CI workflows.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — Vitest 5.0 multi-runtime pyramid config (proposed API, subject to change)
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // Planned V5 default — eliminates per-test mock cleanup boilerplate
    restoreMocks: true, // Breaking: currently defaults to false

    projects: [
      // Unit tests — run on all three runtimes for cross-runtime library validation
      {
        test: {
          name: 'unit:node',
          include: ['src/**/*.unit.test.ts'],
          runtime: 'node',        // V5 proposed runtime field
          sequence: { groupOrder: 1 },
        },
      },
      {
        test: {
          name: 'unit:bun',
          include: ['src/**/*.unit.test.ts'],
          runtime: 'bun',         // Dispatches to Bun runtime
          sequence: { groupOrder: 1 },
        },
      },
      {
        test: {
          name: 'unit:deno',
          include: ['src/**/*.unit.test.ts'],
          runtime: 'deno',        // Dispatches to Deno runtime
          sequence: { groupOrder: 1 },
        },
      },
      // Integration tests — Node.js only (Testcontainers, real DB)
      {
        test: {
          name: 'integration',
          include: ['src/**/*.integration.test.ts'],
          runtime: 'node',
          sequence: { groupOrder: 2 },
          testTimeout: 30_000,
        },
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

**Migration impact for existing projects:** The `restoreMocks` default change is the highest-risk item. Teams must audit all test files for implicit mock reuse across `it()` blocks before upgrading. The automated codemod (planned by the Vitest team) will flag, not fix, affected test cases.

[official: github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/discussions/9664 — Vitest 5 planning discussion (Feb–May 2026)]

### 2. Vitest 5.0 Stabilization — `openTelemetry`, `fsModuleCache`, `viteModuleRunner`, `importDurations`

Vitest 5.0 targets stabilization of four experimental APIs. Each has direct pyramid relevance:

| Experimental API | Pyramid Layer | What it enables when stable |
|-----------------|---------------|------------------------------|
| `openTelemetry` | All levels | Emit OTLP spans per test case → visualize slow integration tests in Grafana/Jaeger |
| `fsModuleCache` | Unit | Persist transformed module cache across Vitest runs → 30–50% unit test warm-start speedup |
| `viteModuleRunner` | Unit/integration | Run test files in the same Vite module graph as the app → eliminates double-transform cost |
| `importDurations` | Unit | Report per-module import time → identify barrel file overhead at the unit level |

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — opting into experimental OpenTelemetry (Vitest 4.x pre-stabilization)
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // Experimental in 4.x — stabilized API expected in 5.0
    openTelemetry: {
      // OTLP HTTP exporter endpoint
      resourceAttributes: {
        'service.name': 'my-app-tests',
        'deployment.environment': process.env.CI ? 'ci' : 'local',
      },
    },
    // importDurations: true — log per-module import time after each run
    // viteModuleRunner: true — use Vite module runner for test isolation
  },
});
```

```typescript
// Reading import durations in a custom Vitest reporter (4.x experimental)
import type { Reporter, File } from 'vitest';

export class ImportDurationReporter implements Reporter {
  onFinished(files: File[]) {
    // importDurations map: moduleId → ms
    // Available when test.importDurations === true
    const slowModules = (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)['__vitest_import_durations__'];
    if (!slowModules) return;

    const entries = Object.entries(slowModules as Record<string, number>)
      .sort(([, a], [, b]) => b - a)
      .slice(0, 10);

    console.log('\n[ImportDurations] Top 10 slowest module imports:');
    for (const [mod, ms] of entries) {
      console.log(`  ${ms.toFixed(0)}ms  ${mod}`);
    }
  }
}
```

[official: github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/discussions/9664 — experimental stabilization target list]

### 3. Node.js 26.1.0 — SuiteContext Enhancements and OTel TracingChannel

Node.js 26.1.0 (May 7, 2026) adds three test runner improvements that matter at the integration and unit pyramid levels.

**SuiteContext enrichment:** `beforeAll` / `afterAll` callbacks now receive a `SuiteContext` with `passed`, `attempt`, and `diagnostic` fields in addition to the existing `signal`. This enables teardown logic that differs based on whether all test cases in the suite passed — useful for keeping integration test databases alive for debugging on failure.

**OpenTelemetry TracingChannel:** The built-in `node:test` runner now publishes to `tracing:node.test:start`, `tracing:node.test:end`, and `tracing:node.test:error` channels. Any OTEL-compatible subscriber (e.g., `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-node-test`) can attach and emit spans, making it possible to visualize test execution timelines in Grafana for CI pipeline analysis.

**`assert` printf-style messages (Node.js 26.0.0 SEMVER-MAJOR):** `node:assert` now accepts printf-style format strings as the third argument to `assert()`, `strictEqual()`, etc. This reduces the need for template literals in integration test assertions.

```typescript
// Node.js 26.1.0 — SuiteContext-aware teardown in integration tests
import { describe, before, after } from 'node:test';
import type { SuiteContext } from 'node:test';

describe('UserRepository integration', () => {
  let dbContainer: StartedPostgreSqlContainer;

  before(async () => {
    dbContainer = await new PostgreSqlContainer('postgres:16').start();
    await runMigrations(dbContainer.getConnectionUri());
  });

  after(async (ctx: SuiteContext) => {
    // New in Node.js 26.1: ctx.passed tells us if all tests in the suite succeeded
    if (!ctx.passed) {
      // Keep container alive for debugging; dump logs
      console.log('[DEBUG] Suite failed — container kept alive for inspection.');
      console.log('[DEBUG] Connection URI:', dbContainer.getConnectionUri());
      // Do NOT stop the container on failure
      return;
    }
    await dbContainer.stop();
  });

  // ... integration test cases
});
```

```typescript
// Node.js 26.1.0 — OTel TracingChannel subscriber for test pyramid observability
import diagnostics_channel from 'node:diagnostics_channel';
import { trace, SpanStatusCode } from '@opentelemetry/api';

const tracer = trace.getTracer('node-test-runner');
const testSpans = new Map<string, ReturnType<typeof tracer.startSpan>>();

diagnostics_channel.subscribe('tracing:node.test:start', (data: unknown) => {
  const { name, nesting } = data as { name: string; nesting: number };
  const span = tracer.startSpan(`test.${nesting === 0 ? 'suite' : 'case'}: ${name}`);
  testSpans.set(name, span);
});

diagnostics_channel.subscribe('tracing:node.test:end', (data: unknown) => {
  const { name, passed } = data as { name: string; passed: boolean };
  const span = testSpans.get(name);
  if (span) {
    span.setStatus({ code: passed ? SpanStatusCode.OK : SpanStatusCode.ERROR });
    span.end();
    testSpans.delete(name);
  }
});
```

[official: nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v26.1.0 — SuiteContext, TracingChannel, test randomization]

### 4. Node.js 26.1.0 — Test Order Randomization for Order-Dependency Detection

Node.js 26.1.0 adds `--test-randomize` and `--test-random-seed=N` flags to `node:test`. This surfaces hidden test-order dependencies in unit and integration test suites without external tooling.

**Pyramid significance:** Order-dependency is the second leading cause of integration test flakiness after shared mutable state. A test case that only passes after a "setup" test case has run is not isolated — it violates the I (Independent) in FIRST principles. Periodic `--test-randomize` runs in CI expose this class of defect.

```typescript
// package.json — CI scripts using order randomization
// {
//   "scripts": {
//     "test:unit": "node --test src/**/*.unit.test.ts",
//     "test:unit:randomize": "node --test --test-randomize src/**/*.unit.test.ts",
//     "test:integration": "node --test src/**/*.integration.test.ts",
//     "test:integration:randomize": "node --test --test-randomize src/**/*.integration.test.ts"
//   }
// }

// GitHub Actions: add a weekly randomized run to surface order-dependencies
// .github/workflows/test-order-health.yml:
// on:
//   schedule:
//     - cron: '0 3 * * 1'  # Every Monday 03:00 UTC
//
// steps:
//   - run: npm run test:unit:randomize
//   - run: npm run test:integration:randomize

// integration test demonstrating order-independence (CORRECT pattern):
import { describe, it } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

describe('OrderRepository', () => {
  it('creates an order', async () => {
    const newOrderId = await createOrder({ userId: 'u1', total: 100 });
    assert.ok(newOrderId, 'order creation should return an ID');
    // Note: do NOT assign to outer variable — other tests should not depend on this
  });

  it('retrieves an order by ID', async () => {
    // CORRECT: creates its own fixture, does not rely on previous test case
    const fixtureId = await createOrder({ userId: 'u2', total: 200 });
    const order = await getOrder(fixtureId);
    assert.strictEqual(order.userId, 'u2');
  });
});

// WRONG pattern (exposed by --test-randomize):
// describe('OrderRepository WRONG', () => {
//   let orderId: string;
//   it('creates an order', async () => { orderId = await createOrder(...); });
//   it('retrieves the order', async () => {
//     const o = await getOrder(orderId); // fails if randomized — orderId may be undefined
//   });
// });
```

### 5. Node.js 26.0.0 — Temporal API for Time-Sensitive Test Cases

Node.js 26.0.0 enables the Temporal API by default (V8 14.6). For test suites that assert on date/time behaviour, `Temporal` provides deterministic, timezone-aware semantics that `new Date()` cannot guarantee.

**Pyramid significance:** Time-sensitive assertions are a leading source of flaky unit and integration test cases. Common failure modes: `new Date()` returns local time in local development and UTC in CI, causing assertions on formatted strings to differ. `Temporal` uses ISO 8601 explicitly, eliminating the local-time/UTC mismatch without mocking.

```typescript
// Unit test — Temporal API for deterministic date assertions (Node.js 26+)
import { describe, it } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

// System under test: formats an order date for display
function formatOrderDate(isoDateString: string): string {
  // Application code using Temporal for timezone-correct formatting
  const date = Temporal.PlainDate.from(isoDateString);
  return date.toLocaleString('en-US', { month: 'long', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' });
}

describe('formatOrderDate', () => {
  it('formats a plain date correctly', () => {
    // CORRECT: Temporal.PlainDate is timezone-free — same result in every environment
    const result = formatOrderDate('2026-05-13');
    assert.strictEqual(result, 'May 13, 2026');
  });

  it('handles year boundaries', () => {
    const result = formatOrderDate('2026-01-01');
    assert.strictEqual(result, 'January 1, 2026');
  });
});
```

```typescript
// Integration test — comparing timestamps with Temporal.Instant (Node.js 26+)
import { describe, it } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

describe('OrderRepository timestamps', () => {
  it('created_at is within 5 seconds of insertion', async () => {
    const beforeInstant = Temporal.Now.instant();
    const orderId = await createOrder({ userId: 'u1', total: 100 });
    const order = await getOrder(orderId);
    const afterInstant = Temporal.Now.instant();

    const createdAt = Temporal.Instant.from(order.createdAt);

    // Temporal.Instant comparison is always UTC — no timezone mismatch
    assert.ok(
      Temporal.Instant.compare(createdAt, beforeInstant) >= 0 &&
      Temporal.Instant.compare(createdAt, afterInstant) <= 0,
      'createdAt %s should be between test start and end', order.createdAt
    );
  });
});
```

[official: nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v26.0.0 — Temporal API enabled by default (V8 14.6)]

### 6. Node.js 26.0.0 — `assert()` Printf-Style Messages for Richer Integration Test Output

Node.js 26.0.0 makes `assert()` accept printf-style format strings as error messages (SEMVER-MAJOR). This reduces string concatenation boilerplate in integration test assertions and produces more readable failure output.

```typescript
// node:assert printf-style messages (Node.js 26.0.0+)
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { describe, it } from 'node:test';

describe('UserRepository.findByEmail integration', () => {
  it('finds an existing user', async () => {
    const user = await userRepo.findByEmail('alice@example.com');

    // OLD (Node.js 24 and earlier — eager string interpolation):
    // assert.ok(user, `Expected to find user but got ${JSON.stringify(user)}`);

    // NEW (Node.js 26+): printf-style — formatted only on failure, not on every pass
    assert.ok(user, 'Expected to find user %s but got %j', 'alice@example.com', user);
    assert.strictEqual(
      user?.email,
      'alice@example.com',
      'Expected email %s but got %s',
      'alice@example.com',
      user?.email
    );
    assert.ok(user?.id, 'User %s should have an id field, got %j', 'alice@example.com', user);
  });

  it('returns null for unknown email', async () => {
    const user = await userRepo.findByEmail('nobody@example.com');
    assert.strictEqual(
      user,
      null,
      'Expected null for unknown email %s, got %j',
      'nobody@example.com',
      user
    );
  });
});
```

**Performance note:** printf-style messages are only formatted when the assertion fails. Template literals (`\`Expected ${JSON.stringify(largeObject)}\``) are evaluated eagerly on every test case execution. For integration tests with large response objects, printf-style messages measurably reduce per-test-case memory allocation overhead.

[official: nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v26.0.0 — printf-style assert messages (SEMVER-MAJOR)]

### 7. Jest 30.4 Stable — `unrs-resolver` Module Resolution Performance Gains

Jest 30's upgrade to `unrs-resolver` (from the Rolldown/Oxc ecosystem) delivers measurable test suite speed and memory improvements without any code changes. The resolver handles TypeScript path aliases, monorepo workspace packages, and ESM `exports` fields natively.

**Real-world benchmark (from Jest 30 release notes):**

| Project type | Time change | Memory change |
|---|---|---|
| Large TypeScript server suite | −37% (1350s → 850s) | −77% (7.8 GB → 1.8 GB) |
| Large client bundle | −10% | −20% |

```typescript
// jest.config.ts — Jest 30 migration: what you no longer need vs what changed
import type { Config } from 'jest';

const config: Config = {
  // REMOVED: moduleNameMapper for workspace packages (unrs-resolver handles exports field natively)
  // REMOVED: resolver: 'jest-resolve-alias' (unrs-resolver handles TypeScript path aliases)

  // KEEP: testEnvironment — jsdom upgraded from v21 to v26 in Jest 30
  testEnvironment: 'jsdom',

  // RECOMMENDED: enable globalsCleanup to prevent window/document state leakage
  // between test files (default 'soft' emits warnings; 'on' enforces cleanup)
  testEnvironmentOptions: {
    globalsCleanup: 'on',
  },

  transform: {
    '^.+\\.tsx?$': ['ts-jest', { useESM: true }],
  },

  // MIGRATION REQUIRED for jsdom v26: window.location is now non-configurable
  // Old: delete window.location; window.location = { href: '...' }
  // New: Object.defineProperty(window, 'location', { configurable: true, value: {...} })
};

export default config;
```

```typescript
// Jest 30 — `using` keyword for automatic spy cleanup (replaces afterEach restore)
import { describe, it, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import * as mailer from './mailer.js';

describe('sendWelcomeEmail', () => {
  it('calls the mailer with the correct subject', () => {
    // `using` keyword: spy is automatically restored when the test case block exits
    using spy = jest.spyOn(mailer, 'sendMail').mockResolvedValue({ messageId: 'test' });

    sendWelcomeEmail('alice@example.com');

    expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ subject: 'Welcome to the platform' })
    );
    // No afterEach(() => spy.mockRestore()) needed
  });
});
```

### 8. Playwright `captureGitInfo` — Embedding Commit Context in HTML Reports

Playwright v1.60 adds `testConfig.captureGitInfo` to automatically embed Git commit hash, branch, and diff information into HTML and blob reports. This is a CI quality-of-life improvement: when an e2e test suite fails on a PR, the HTML report already contains which commit introduced the failure without consulting the CI log.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — captureGitInfo for enriched HTML reports
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  // Embed git commit, branch, and diff info into the HTML/blob report
  captureGitInfo: {
    commit: true,
    branch: true,
    // Optional: include the diff stat for the changed files (useful for bisecting)
    diff: process.env.CI === 'true',
  },

  reporter: [
    ['html', { open: 'never', outputFolder: 'playwright-report' }],
    // Blob reporter for sharded runs — captureGitInfo applies to blob reports too
    ['blob', { outputDir: 'blob-report' }],
  ],

  use: {
    baseURL: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
    trace: 'on-first-retry',
    screenshot: 'on-first-failure',
  },

  projects: [
    { name: 'chromium', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] } },
    { name: 'firefox',  use: { ...devices['Desktop Firefox'] } },
  ],

  // Merge sharded blob reports into a single HTML report in CI:
  // npx playwright merge-reports --reporter html ./all-blob-reports
});
```

**Pyramid use case:** E2e test suites are the last CI gate before deployment. When an e2e gate fails, `captureGitInfo` reduces time-to-diagnose by making the commit context visible without navigating out of the test report.

### 9. Playwright v1.60 — `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` for Form Validation E2E Tests

Playwright v1.60 adds `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` to the assertion library. This assertion verifies that an ARIA `aria-errormessage` attribute correctly points to a visible error element — a common gap in form validation e2e test cases that previously required manual chaining.

**Pyramid significance:** Form validation logic belongs at the unit level (Zod schema), the integration level (HTTP 400 response shape), and the e2e level (UI error display and ARIA accessibility). `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage` makes the e2e layer complete without custom helpers.

```typescript
// e2e test — form validation with toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage (Playwright v1.60)
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Registration form validation', () => {
  test('shows an accessible error for duplicate email', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');
    await page.getByLabel('Email address').fill('existing@example.com');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create account' }).click();

    const emailInput = page.getByLabel('Email address');

    // v1.60 — checks aria-invalid="true" AND aria-errormessage points to visible element
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(
      'This email address is already registered'
    );

    // Complementary: also assert the error element is visible to sighted users
    await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText('already registered');
  });

  test('clears error state when valid email is entered', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');
    await page.getByLabel('Email address').fill('existing@example.com');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create account' }).click();

    // Confirm error state
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Email address')).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');

    // Correct the input
    await page.getByLabel('Email address').clear();
    await page.getByLabel('Email address').fill('new@example.com');
    await page.getByLabel('Email address').blur();

    // Assert error is cleared
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Email address')).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Email address')).not.toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage();
  });
});
```

[official: playwright.dev/docs/release-notes — v1.60 toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage assertion]

### 10. Vitest `detectAsyncLeaks` — Catching Open Handles at the Integration Level

Vitest 4.1 adds `detectAsyncLeaks: true` as a test configuration option. When enabled, Vitest reports any pending async operations (HTTP servers, database connections, timers) that were not cleaned up after a test case or suite completes. This catches a common integration test anti-pattern: tests that spin up a service in `beforeAll` and forget to stop it in `afterAll`.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — enable leak detection for integration project only
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    projects: [
      {
        test: {
          name: 'unit',
          include: ['src/**/*.unit.test.ts'],
          // detectAsyncLeaks not needed at unit level (no real I/O)
        },
      },
      {
        test: {
          name: 'integration',
          include: ['src/**/*.integration.test.ts'],
          // Enable for integration layer — surfaces unclosed DB connections, HTTP servers
          detectAsyncLeaks: true,
          testTimeout: 30_000,
        },
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

```typescript
// integration test — correct server lifecycle with detectAsyncLeaks enabled
import { describe, it, beforeAll, afterAll, expect } from 'vitest';
import { createApp } from '../src/app.js';
import type { Server } from 'node:http';

describe('health check endpoint', () => {
  let server: Server;
  let baseUrl: string;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    const app = createApp();
    await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      server = app.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve);
    });
    const address = server.address() as { port: number };
    baseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${address.port}`;
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    // REQUIRED when detectAsyncLeaks:true — failure to close will be reported as a leak
    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      server.close((err) => (err ? reject(err) : resolve()));
    });
  });

  it('returns 200 OK', async () => {
    const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/health`);
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
  });
});
```

**Pyramid anti-pattern caught by this flag:** `beforeAll(() => server.listen())` without `afterAll(() => server.close())` causes CI jobs to hang after the test file completes. `detectAsyncLeaks` surfaces this immediately with a clear error message identifying the source.

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4-1 — detectAsyncLeaks configuration option]

### 11. Vitest `coverage.changed` — Per-PR Coverage Delta Without Slowing CI

Vitest 4.1's `coverage.changed` option limits coverage reporting to only the files modified in the current git diff. This solves the "coverage report takes longer than the tests" problem that plagues large codebases where full Istanbul/V8 instrumentation is expensive.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — per-PR coverage delta targeting changed files only
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      enabled: process.env.COVERAGE === 'true',

      // Only instrument and report changed files (git diff based)
      // Full coverage still runs on the main branch nightly
      changed: process.env.CI_EVENT === 'pull_request',

      // Thresholds still apply to the changed subset
      thresholds: {
        lines: 80,
        branches: 75,
        functions: 80,
        statements: 80,
        // perFile: true — enforce thresholds per changed file, not aggregate
        perFile: true,
      },

      exclude: [
        '**/*.test.ts',
        '**/*.spec.ts',
        '**/*.integration.test.ts',
        'vitest.config.ts',
        'src/types/**',
      ],
    },
  },
});
```

**Pyramid strategy:** Run `coverage.changed: true` on every PR (fast, relevant feedback). Run `coverage.changed: false` (full coverage) on the main branch nightly. This keeps PR feedback loops under 60 seconds for large projects while still enforcing coverage gates for all production code.

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4-1 — coverage.changed option]

### 12. Vitest `vi.defineHelper` — Clean Stack Traces in Custom Assertion Libraries

Vitest 4.1's `vi.defineHelper` wraps utility functions so that their internal frames are excluded from test failure stack traces. Without this, custom assertion helpers show their internal `expect` call frames on failure rather than the test case line that called them.

```typescript
// test-helpers/assert-order.ts — using vi.defineHelper for clean stack traces
import { vi, expect } from 'vitest';

// Without vi.defineHelper: stack trace points to line inside assertOrderShape
// With vi.defineHelper: stack trace points to the test case that called assertOrderShape

export const assertOrderShape = vi.defineHelper(
  function assertOrderShape(order: unknown): asserts order is {
    id: string;
    userId: string;
    total: number;
    status: 'pending' | 'confirmed' | 'shipped';
  } {
    expect(order).toMatchObject({
      id: expect.any(String),
      userId: expect.any(String),
      total: expect.any(Number),
      status: expect.stringMatching(/^(pending|confirmed|shipped)$/),
    });
  }
);
```

```typescript
// integration test — clean failure output with vi.defineHelper
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { assertOrderShape } from '../test-helpers/assert-order.js';

describe('OrderRepository', () => {
  it('returns a well-formed order object', async () => {
    const order = await orderRepo.findById('o1');

    // Stack trace on failure: points to THIS line, not inside assertOrderShape
    assertOrderShape(order);

    // Continue with specific assertions after shape validation
    expect(order.status).toBe('confirmed');
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** Well-factored assertion helpers are the DRY mechanism for integration test cases that share complex shape validation. Without `vi.defineHelper`, failure stack traces inside helpers mislead developers into looking at the helper code rather than the failing test case.

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4-1 — vi.defineHelper API]

### 13. Vitest `test.tags` — Selective CI Execution Across Pyramid Levels  [community]

Vitest 4.1's test tag system (`test.tags` + `--tags-filter` CLI) enables precise selection of test cases for different CI stages. Teams can mark test cases with pyramid-level and scope tags, then run only the relevant subset in each CI job.

```typescript
// Unit test tagged for selective CI execution
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';

describe('PriceCalculator', () => {
  it('applies percentage discount', { tags: ['unit', 'fast', 'pricing'] }, () => {
    const result = applyDiscount(100, 0.15);
    expect(result).toBe(85);
  });

  it('rejects negative prices', { tags: ['unit', 'fast', 'pricing', 'validation'] }, () => {
    expect(() => applyDiscount(-50, 0.1)).toThrow('Price must be non-negative');
  });
});
```

```typescript
// Integration test tagged for selective CI execution
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';

describe('OrderService.createOrder', () => {
  it('persists order to database', { tags: ['integration', 'slow', 'orders', 'db'] }, async () => {
    const orderId = await orderService.createOrder({ userId: 'u1', items: [] });
    expect(orderId).toMatch(/^ord-/);
  });

  it('publishes order created event', { tags: ['integration', 'slow', 'orders', 'events'] }, async () => {
    await orderService.createOrder({ userId: 'u1', items: [] });
    expect(eventBus.published).toContainEqual(
      expect.objectContaining({ type: 'order.created' })
    );
  });
});
```

```bash
# CI pipeline — pyramid-level tag filtering stages
# Stage 1: unit tests only (fast gate, < 30s target)
vitest run --tags-filter="unit"

# Stage 2: integration tests (slower gate, < 3 min target)
vitest run --tags-filter="integration"

# Stage 3: browser/component tests (requires browser install)
vitest run --tags-filter="browser"

# Local: run only fast tests regardless of level
vitest --tags-filter="fast"

# Local: skip slow tests during development iteration
vitest --tags-filter="!slow"

# CI: run everything except known-flaky tests under quarantine
vitest run --tags-filter="!flaky"
```

### 14. Property-Based Testing with `@fast-check/vitest` at the Unit Level  [community]

`@fast-check/vitest` provides a `test.prop()` API that integrates property-based testing natively into Vitest's test runner. Property-based test cases belong at the unit level and are the most effective way to find edge cases that example-based test cases miss.

```typescript
// Installation: npm install --save-dev @fast-check/vitest fast-check
// Note: @fast-check/vitest 0.4+ is ESM-only — requires "type": "module" in package.json
//       or .mts extension for vitest.config

// unit test — property-based testing with test.prop()
import { describe } from 'vitest';
import { test } from '@fast-check/vitest';
import * as fc from 'fast-check';
import { parsePositiveInt } from '../src/utils/parse.js';

describe('parsePositiveInt', () => {
  // Property: any non-negative integer stringified and parsed should round-trip
  test.prop([fc.nat()])(
    'round-trips non-negative integers',
    (n) => {
      const result = parsePositiveInt(String(n));
      return result === n;
    }
  );

  // Property: non-numeric strings always return null
  test.prop([fc.string().filter(s => !/^\d+$/.test(s))])(
    'returns null for non-numeric input',
    (s) => {
      return parsePositiveInt(s) === null;
    }
  );

  // Property: valid results are always non-negative
  test.prop([fc.nat()])(
    'result is always >= 0 for digit strings',
    (n) => {
      const result = parsePositiveInt(String(n));
      return result !== null && result >= 0;
    }
  );
});
```

**ESM migration gotcha:** `@fast-check/vitest` 0.4+ dropped CommonJS support entirely. Projects using `require('@fast-check/vitest')` in a CJS Vitest setup will receive `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` on upgrade. The fix is to convert to ESM (`"type": "module"` in `package.json` or rename config to `vitest.config.mts`). [community: fast-check community reports, vitest-dev/vitest GitHub issues May 2026]

[community: @fast-check/vitest GitHub releases — 0.4+ ESM-only migration note]

### 15. MSW v2.14+ WebSocket Handler — Integration Testing WebSocket Endpoints

MSW (Mock Service Worker) v2.14+ adds WebSocket interception support via the `ws` export. This enables integration test cases that verify WebSocket behavior at the Node.js level without spinning up a real WebSocket server — closing a significant gap that previously forced teams to push WebSocket coverage to the e2e layer.

```typescript
// Integration test — MSW WebSocket interception (MSW v2.14+)
import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterAll, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node';
import { ws } from 'msw';

const wsMock = ws.link('ws://localhost:3001/events');

const server = setupServer(
  wsMock.addEventListener('connection', ({ client }) => {
    // Simulate the server sending a connection acknowledgement
    client.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'connected', sessionId: 'test-session-1' }));

    client.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
      const msg = JSON.parse(event.data as string);
      if (msg.type === 'subscribe') {
        client.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'subscribed', channel: msg.channel }));
      }
    });
  })
);

beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' }));
afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers());
afterAll(() => server.close());

describe('EventStream WebSocket client', () => {
  it('receives a connection acknowledgement on connect', async () => {
    const messages: unknown[] = [];
    const client = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:3001/events');

    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      client.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
        messages.push(JSON.parse(event.data));
        resolve();
      });
      client.addEventListener('error', reject);
    });

    client.close();
    expect(messages[0]).toEqual(expect.objectContaining({ type: 'connected' }));
  });

  it('receives subscription confirmation after subscribing', async () => {
    const client = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:3001/events');
    const confirmations: unknown[] = [];

    await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      client.addEventListener('open', () => {
        client.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'subscribe', channel: 'orders' }));
      });
      client.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
        const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);
        if (msg.type === 'subscribed') {
          confirmations.push(msg);
          resolve();
        }
      });
    });

    client.close();
    expect(confirmations[0]).toEqual(
      expect.objectContaining({ type: 'subscribed', channel: 'orders' })
    );
  });
});
```

[community: mswjs.io release notes — WebSocket interception support (v2.14+)]

### 16. Jest 30 `jsdom` v26 — Fixing `window.location` Mocking After the Breaking Change

Jest 30 upgrades `jsdom` from v21 to v26. The most common integration-level breakage is `window.location` mocking. In jsdom v26, `window.location` is non-configurable and non-writable, so the widespread `delete window.location; window.location = {...}` pattern throws a `TypeError`.

```typescript
// BROKEN in Jest 30 / jsdom v26 — common pre-v30 pattern:
// delete window.location;
// window.location = { href: 'https://example.com/dashboard', assign: jest.fn() };
// ^^ TypeError: Cannot delete property 'location' of #<Window>

// CORRECT in Jest 30 / jsdom v26:
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from '@jest/globals';

describe('Navigation guard', () => {
  const originalDescriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(window, 'location');

  beforeEach(() => {
    Object.defineProperty(window, 'location', {
      configurable: true,
      writable: true,
      value: {
        href: 'https://example.com',
        assign: jest.fn(),
        replace: jest.fn(),
        reload: jest.fn(),
        origin: 'https://example.com',
        pathname: '/',
        search: '',
        hash: '',
      },
    });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    if (originalDescriptor) {
      Object.defineProperty(window, 'location', originalDescriptor);
    }
  });

  it('redirects unauthenticated users to /login', () => {
    const guard = new NavigationGuard({ authenticated: false });
    guard.checkAccess('/dashboard');
    expect(window.location.assign).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/login');
  });

  it('allows authenticated users to proceed', () => {
    const guard = new NavigationGuard({ authenticated: true });
    const blocked = guard.checkAccess('/dashboard');
    expect(blocked).toBe(false);
    expect(window.location.assign).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});
```

**Alternative: configure the jsdom URL at the test environment level** to avoid `window.location` mocking entirely for URL-dependent unit tests:

```typescript
// jest.config.ts — set testURL to avoid location mocking in most tests
const config: Config = {
  testEnvironment: 'jsdom',
  testEnvironmentOptions: {
    url: 'https://example.com',
    globalsCleanup: 'on',
  },
};
```

[official: jestjs.io/docs/upgrading-to-jest30 — jsdom v26 migration section]

### 17. Vitest `aroundAll` Hook — Database Transaction Wrapping for Integration Tests  [community]

Vitest 4.1's `aroundAll` hook (sibling to `aroundEach`) wraps the entire suite inside a single async context. The canonical use case is wrapping all integration tests in a database transaction that rolls back after the suite — eliminating `afterEach` data cleanup code without requiring truncation queries.

```typescript
// test-setup/db-transaction.ts — global transaction rollback via aroundAll
// (setupFiles entry for integration project in vitest.config.ts)
import { aroundAll } from 'vitest';
import { pool } from '../src/db/pool.js';

// Wrap every integration suite in a transaction that auto-rolls-back
// Eliminates afterEach(() => deleteAll(...)) boilerplate for DB state cleanup
aroundAll(async (runSuite) => {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  await client.query('BEGIN');

  // Make the transactional client available globally for test cases
  (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__testDbClient = client;

  try {
    await runSuite();
  } finally {
    await client.query('ROLLBACK');
    client.release();
    delete (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__testDbClient;
  }
});
```

```typescript
// integration test — uses the transactional client; no teardown required
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import type { PoolClient } from 'pg';

describe('UserRepository.create', () => {
  function getClient(): PoolClient {
    return (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__testDbClient as PoolClient;
  }

  it('inserts a user row', async () => {
    const result = await getClient().query(
      "INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ('test@example.com') RETURNING id"
    );
    expect(result.rows[0].id).toBeDefined();
    // Transaction auto-rolls-back in aroundAll teardown — no DELETE needed
  });

  it('enforces unique email constraint', async () => {
    await getClient().query("INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ('dup@example.com')");
    await expect(
      getClient().query("INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ('dup@example.com')")
    ).rejects.toThrow(/unique constraint/);
  });
});
```

**Critical constraint:** `aroundAll` wraps the entire suite file. Vitest's default worker pool (`pool: 'forks'`) spawns separate processes — a transaction acquired in one process is not visible to other processes. Set `pool: 'vmThreads'` or `singleThread: true` for the integration project to ensure all test cases share a single process and the same DB connection. [community: Vitest 4.1 aroundAll early adopter feedback, vitest-dev/vitest GitHub issue tracker]

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4-1 — aroundAll/aroundEach hooks]

### 18. Playwright v1.60 — `webSocketRoute.protocols()` for Protocol-Level E2E Tests

Playwright v1.60 adds `webSocketRoute.protocols()` to the WebSocket route API. This allows e2e test cases to inspect or assert on WebSocket subprotocol negotiation — critical for applications that use protocol-level versioning (e.g., `graphql-ws`, STOMP over WebSocket).

```typescript
// e2e test — WebSocket subprotocol inspection and assertion (Playwright v1.60)
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('chat WebSocket negotiates the correct subprotocol', async ({ page, context }) => {
  let observedProtocols: string[] = [];

  // Intercept WebSocket connections from the page
  await context.routeWebSocket(/\/chat/, (wsRoute) => {
    // Inspect the requested protocols from the browser client
    observedProtocols = wsRoute.protocols();

    // Accept with the preferred protocol and forward to the real server
    wsRoute.connect();
  });

  await page.goto('/chat');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Connect' }).click();

  // Wait for the connection status to update in the UI
  await expect(page.getByTestId('connection-status')).toHaveText('Connected');

  // Assert that the correct subprotocol was requested
  expect(observedProtocols).toContain('chat.v2');
  expect(observedProtocols).not.toContain('chat.v1'); // old clients should not request v1
});

test('gracefully downgrades to v1 if server only supports v1', async ({ page, context }) => {
  await context.routeWebSocket(/\/chat/, (wsRoute) => {
    const protocols = wsRoute.protocols();
    // Simulate a v1-only server: reject v2, accept v1
    if (!protocols.includes('chat.v1')) {
      wsRoute.close(1002, 'Protocol not supported');
      return;
    }
    wsRoute.connect();
  });

  await page.goto('/chat');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Connect' }).click();

  // Application should show a downgrade notice
  await expect(page.getByTestId('protocol-notice')).toContainText('Legacy mode');
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** WebSocket protocol negotiation cannot be tested at the unit or integration levels because it requires a real browser WebSocket client. This is a genuine e2e-only test scenario — an example of behaviour that legitimately belongs at the top of the pyramid and justifies e2e investment.

[official: playwright.dev/docs/release-notes — v1.60 webSocketRoute.protocols()]

### Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 24)  [community]

70. **Vitest 5.0 `restoreMocks: true` default will silently break test cases that share mock implementations across `it()` blocks** [community] — Any test file that calls `vi.fn().mockImplementation()` in a `beforeAll` and expects the mock to persist across multiple `it()` blocks will fail after the Vitest 5.0 upgrade: the mock is restored after the first test case. Audit pattern before upgrading: search for `beforeAll.*mockImplementation\|beforeAll.*mockReturnValue` — each hit needs the mock setup moved to `beforeEach` or into each `it()` block. [community: vitest-dev/vitest/discussions/9664 — mock defaults breaking change discussion]

71. **Node.js 26.0.0 removes `--experimental-transform-types` — CI scripts that pass this flag will fail with "unknown flag" error** [community] — Teams that added `--experimental-transform-types` explicitly to `package.json` test scripts on Node.js 24 will see a fatal startup error on Node.js 26 upgrade (the flag causes an exit-1 before any test runs). Remove the flag from all `node` invocations in CI and `package.json` scripts before upgrading the Node.js version in your Docker image or toolchain. [official: nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v26.0.0]

72. **Jest 30 `globalsCleanup: 'on'` + React Testing Library `cleanup` causes double-cleanup errors** [community] — RTL registers an `afterEach` cleanup handler automatically. When Jest 30's `globalsCleanup: 'on'` is also enabled, both cleanup mechanisms fire and can produce `act()` warnings or `"Cannot update a component while rendering a different component"` errors. Fix: set `globalsCleanup: 'soft'` if using RTL, or explicitly call `cleanup()` in `afterEach` yourself and disable RTL's auto-cleanup via `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = false`. [community: Jest 30 migration thread, react-testing-library GitHub issues May 2026]

73. **Playwright `captureGitInfo` fails silently in Docker containers built without a `.git` directory** [community] — `captureGitInfo: { commit: true }` calls `git rev-parse HEAD` at test startup. In Docker containers that `COPY` only built artifacts (no `.git`), the git command fails silently and `commit` is `null` in the report — which can crash downstream tooling that requires a non-null commit field. Guard pattern: `captureGitInfo: process.env.GITHUB_SHA ? { commit: true } : false`. [community: Playwright GitHub discussions — captureGitInfo Docker adoption]

74. **Vitest `aroundAll` with the default `pool: 'forks'` isolates transactions per process — all worker processes see no data** [community] — A database transaction acquired in `aroundAll` is held by the process that runs the `aroundAll` wrapper; Vitest's forked worker processes use a different database connection and see an empty database (under `READ COMMITTED`). To use transaction-rollback isolation, set `pool: 'vmThreads'` or `singleThread: true` for the integration project so test cases and the `aroundAll` wrapper run in the same process and share one connection. [community: Vitest 4.1 aroundAll early adopter feedback]

75. **`@fast-check/vitest` 0.4+ is ESM-only — `^0.3.0` version ranges silently upgrade and break CommonJS test projects** [community] — npm's semver allows `^0.3.0` to resolve to `0.4.x` when running `npm update`. Teams using `require('@fast-check/vitest')` in CJS Vitest setups receive `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` only at test runtime. Pin to `~0.3` until you can migrate to ESM, or add an `overrides` entry in `package.json` to lock the version. [community: fast-check 4.x release notes, npm semver behavior]

76. **Node.js 26.1.0 `--test-randomize` without a captured seed makes CI failures non-reproducible** [community] — `--test-randomize` uses a random seed by default; the seed is printed in test output but is lost when CI log output is truncated. Always capture the seed via `--test-random-seed` for reproducibility: use `--test-random-seed=$(date +%s)` for daily stability runs (same seed within a day) and store it as a CI artifact, or use a content-hash based seed (`--test-random-seed=$(shasum -a 256 src | head -c 8)`) to tie the seed to the source code state. [community: Node.js 26.1.0 early adopter reports]

77. **Vitest `detectAsyncLeaks: true` reports false positives for the `supertest(app)` pattern** [community] — `supertest`'s `request(app)` creates a temporary HTTP server that binds to a random port and is supposed to close after each request completes. On slow CI machines, the server is sometimes not fully closed before the leak detector fires, producing a spurious "open handles: tcp server" report. Fix: switch to `supertest.agent(app)` with an explicit `.end()` callback, or use `app.listen(0)` + explicit `server.close()` in `afterAll` instead of passing the express `app` directly to `supertest`. [community: Vitest 4.1 detectAsyncLeaks adoption thread, supertest GitHub issues]

## Cycle 25 — 2026-05-13

<!-- sources: WebFetch: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4-1, vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4, jestjs.io/blog (Jest 30), jestjs.io/docs/upgrading-to-jest30, playwright.dev/docs/release-notes, nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/test.html, stryker-mutator.io/blog, dev.to/t/testing, github.com/dubzzz/fast-check | training-knowledge synthesis -->

### 1. Jest 30 `using` Keyword for Automatic Spy Cleanup  [official]

Jest 30 adopts the TC39 Explicit Resource Management proposal (`using` / `Symbol.dispose`). Spies declared with `using` are automatically restored when the block exits — no manual `mockRestore()` or `afterEach` cleanup required. This eliminates the integration-test anti-pattern of spy leakage across test cases in the same file, which was a major source of order-dependent flakiness at the unit level.

```typescript
// Before Jest 30 — manual restore required
import { describe, it, expect, afterEach, jest } from '@jest/globals';

describe('PaymentService', () => {
  let spy: jest.SpyInstance;

  afterEach(() => {
    spy?.mockRestore(); // easy to forget → spy leaks to next test case
  });

  it('calls Stripe when amount > 0', () => {
    spy = jest.spyOn(StripeClient.prototype, 'charge');
    spy.mockResolvedValue({ id: 'ch_1' });
    // ...
  });
});

// Jest 30 — automatic restore via `using`
describe('PaymentService', () => {
  it('calls Stripe when amount > 0', () => {
    using spy = jest.spyOn(StripeClient.prototype, 'charge');
    spy.mockResolvedValue({ id: 'ch_1' });
    const svc = new PaymentService();
    svc.charge(100, 'tok_visa');
    expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(100, 'tok_visa');
    // spy automatically restored when `using` block exits
  });

  it('skips Stripe when amount is 0', () => {
    using spy = jest.spyOn(StripeClient.prototype, 'charge');
    const svc = new PaymentService();
    svc.charge(0, 'tok_visa');
    expect(spy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** At the unit test level, leaked spies are the root cause of "test case passes in isolation, fails in suite" problems. `using` makes spy scope explicit and guaranteed. Requires TypeScript `target: 'es2022'` and `lib: ['es2022']` (or higher) to compile; add `"useUnknownInCatchVariables": false` if your Jest config uses CommonJS transforms.

[official: jestjs.io/blog — Jest 30 release, Symbol.dispose support]

---

### 2. Jest 30 `expect.arrayOf` Matcher for Homogeneous Arrays  [official]

A new asymmetric matcher validates every element of an array against a condition in a single assertion. Previously, teams wrote `.forEach` loops or spread `.toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([...]))` assertions to validate API response arrays at the integration test level.

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from '@jest/globals';
import { fetchProducts } from '../src/api/products';

describe('GET /products integration test case', () => {
  it('returns an array where every item has a numeric price', async () => {
    const products = await fetchProducts({ category: 'electronics' });

    // Before Jest 30 — verbose loop:
    // products.forEach(p => expect(typeof p.price).toBe('number'));

    // Jest 30 — single assertion:
    expect(products).toEqual(
      expect.arrayOf(
        expect.objectContaining({
          id: expect.any(String),
          name: expect.any(String),
          price: expect.any(Number),
          inStock: expect.any(Boolean),
        })
      )
    );
  });

  it('returns an empty array (not null) when no products match', async () => {
    const products = await fetchProducts({ category: '__nonexistent__' });
    // arrayOf works on empty arrays — confirms the shape contract holds vacuously
    expect(products).toEqual(expect.arrayOf(expect.any(Object)));
    expect(products).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** `expect.arrayOf` is especially valuable at the integration test level for validating OpenAPI-contracted response shapes. A single assertion on the whole collection detects partial failures (e.g., one item missing a required field) that a spot-check on `products[0]` would miss.

[official: jestjs.io/blog — Jest 30 new matchers]

---

### 3. Jest 30 `jest.advanceTimersToNextFrame()` for Animation-Dependent Unit Tests  [official]

`jest.advanceTimersToNextFrame()` advances fake timers precisely to the next `requestAnimationFrame` callback without requiring a hardcoded millisecond estimate. This enables reliable unit test cases for animation logic, scroll-based hooks, and canvas rendering pipelines that previously required brittle `jest.advanceTimersByTime(16)` hacks (assuming 60 fps).

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import { AnimationController } from '../src/ui/AnimationController';

describe('AnimationController', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    jest.useFakeTimers();
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    jest.useRealTimers();
  });

  it('applies the next animation frame on tick()', () => {
    const ctrl = new AnimationController({ from: 0, to: 100, duration: 300 });
    ctrl.start();

    // No magic numbers — frame-accurate advance
    jest.advanceTimersToNextFrame();
    expect(ctrl.currentValue).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(ctrl.currentValue).toBeLessThan(100);
  });

  it('reaches target value after all frames complete', () => {
    const ctrl = new AnimationController({ from: 0, to: 100, duration: 300 });
    ctrl.start();

    jest.runAllTimers(); // drives all rAF callbacks to completion
    expect(ctrl.currentValue).toBe(100);
    expect(ctrl.isComplete).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** Animation logic previously required browser-level (e2e) test cases because `requestAnimationFrame` wasn't reliably mockable in jsdom. `jest.advanceTimersToNextFrame()` brings this coverage down to the unit level, following the pyramid's primary principle: push test cases to the cheapest capable level.

[official: jestjs.io/blog — Jest 30, advanceTimersToNextFrame from @sinonjs/fake-timers v13]

---

### 4. Jest 30 `jest.onGenerateMock()` for Centralized Auto-Mock Customization  [official]

`jest.onGenerateMock(callback)` registers a global hook that runs every time Jest auto-generates a mock from a module. This removes the repetitive `jest.mock('./SomeService', () => ({ ... }))` boilerplate found in every integration test file that imports the same dependency.

```typescript
// jest.setup.ts — run once for the entire integration test suite
import { jest } from '@jest/globals';
import type { DatabaseClient } from './src/db/DatabaseClient';

// Customize every auto-mock of DatabaseClient globally
jest.onGenerateMock((modulePath, moduleMock) => {
  if (modulePath.includes('DatabaseClient')) {
    const mock = moduleMock as jest.Mocked<DatabaseClient>;
    mock.query = jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({ rows: [], rowCount: 0 });
    mock.transaction = jest.fn().mockImplementation(async (fn) => fn(mock));
    mock.close = jest.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  }
  return moduleMock;
});

// Individual test file — no need to repeat mock setup
import { describe, it, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import { UserRepository } from '../src/repositories/UserRepository';

jest.mock('../src/db/DatabaseClient'); // auto-mock; onGenerateMock hook applies

describe('UserRepository', () => {
  it('queries the correct table for a user by email', async () => {
    const repo = new UserRepository();
    await repo.findByEmail('alice@example.com');
    // The globally-configured mock captures the call
    expect(DatabaseClient.prototype.query).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = $1',
      ['alice@example.com']
    );
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** `jest.onGenerateMock` enforces consistent mock defaults across all unit test files that auto-mock the same infrastructure dependencies. It prevents divergence where one test file stubs `DatabaseClient.query` differently from another, causing integration-test behavior to be misrepresented at the unit level.

[official: jestjs.io/blog — Jest 30 jest.onGenerateMock]

---

### 5. Jest 30 Configurable Retry Timing: `waitBeforeRetry` and `retryImmediately`  [official]

Jest 30 adds retry timing options to `jest.retryTimes()`. `waitBeforeRetry: N` inserts a delay between attempts (useful for integration test cases that wait on eventual consistency); `retryImmediately: true` retries without delay for transient assertion failures.

```typescript
// jest.config.ts — project-level retry configuration
export default {
  projects: [
    {
      displayName: 'unit',
      testMatch: ['**/*.unit.test.ts'],
      // No retries for unit test cases — flakiness here is a code defect
    },
    {
      displayName: 'integration',
      testMatch: ['**/*.integration.test.ts'],
      testEnvironment: 'node',
      // Wait 500 ms between retries for eventual-consistency assertions
      // (e.g., event-sourced projections that update asynchronously)
    },
  ],
};

// integration test case — retry with delay for projection lag
import { describe, it, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';

// Applied per-test-file for this integration project
jest.retryTimes(3, { waitBeforeRetry: 500 });

describe('OrderProjection (event-sourced)', () => {
  it('reflects status change within 1.5 s after event is published', async () => {
    await eventBus.publish(new OrderShippedEvent({ orderId: 'o-123' }));

    // Projection may lag; retry up to 3 times with 500 ms between attempts
    const order = await orderProjection.getById('o-123');
    expect(order.status).toBe('shipped');
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** Retry configuration at the integration level should use `waitBeforeRetry` to accommodate async propagation. At the unit level, retries should be disabled entirely — a flaky unit test case signals a test defect (timing assumption, shared state), not an environmental transient. The pyramid principle: only the level closest to the real system should tolerate timing variability.

[official: jestjs.io/docs/jest-object#jestretrytimenumretries-options — Jest 30 retry options]

---

### 6. Vitest `aroundEach` Hook for Scoped Database Transactions  [official]

Vitest 4.1 `aroundEach` wraps each test case in a single generator function that owns both setup and teardown. Combined with database transaction rollback, it provides the cleanest integration test isolation pattern available in the TypeScript ecosystem: each test case runs inside a transaction that is unconditionally rolled back, leaving no residual data.

```typescript
// vitest.integration.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    include: ['**/*.integration.test.ts'],
    pool: 'vmThreads',        // Required: aroundEach transaction must share the connection
    singleThread: true,       // Simpler alternative for small integration suites
    setupFiles: ['./test/setup-db.ts'],
  },
});

// test/setup-db.ts — shared test db client
import { pool } from '../src/db';
export { pool };

// test/helpers/transactionFixture.ts
import { test } from 'vitest';
import { pool } from '../setup-db';
import { PoolClient } from 'pg';

export const dbTest = test.extend<{ client: PoolClient }>({
  client: async function* ({ task }, use) {
    const client = await pool.connect();
    await client.query('BEGIN');
    try {
      await use(client);   // test case runs here
    } finally {
      await client.query('ROLLBACK');
      client.release();
    }
  },
});

// user-repository.integration.test.ts
import { expect } from 'vitest';
import { dbTest } from '../helpers/transactionFixture';
import { UserRepository } from '../../src/repositories/UserRepository';

dbTest('creates a user and assigns a generated UUID', async ({ client }) => {
  const repo = new UserRepository(client);
  const user = await repo.create({ email: 'bob@example.com', role: 'viewer' });

  expect(user.id).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
  expect(user.email).toBe('bob@example.com');
  // ROLLBACK fires automatically — no cleanup needed, no data pollution between test cases
});

dbTest('prevents duplicate email registration', async ({ client }) => {
  const repo = new UserRepository(client);
  await repo.create({ email: 'alice@example.com', role: 'admin' });

  await expect(
    repo.create({ email: 'alice@example.com', role: 'viewer' })
  ).rejects.toThrow('unique constraint');
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** Transaction-rollback isolation removes the single biggest source of order-dependent integration test failures: residual database state from previous test cases. This technique was possible before Vitest 4.1 but required manual wrapping; `aroundEach` makes the pattern first-class and eliminates the need to coordinate teardown across `beforeEach`/`afterEach` pairs.

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4-1 — aroundEach/aroundAll hooks]

---

### 7. Vitest `viteModuleRunner: false` — Native Node.js Imports in Integration Tests  [official]

Vitest 4.1 introduced the experimental `viteModuleRunner: false` option to run test cases using native Node.js `import()` instead of Vite's transform sandbox. For integration test cases that test compiled build artifacts or native Node.js modules, this eliminates Vite's module resolution layer and produces closer-to-production behaviour.

```typescript
// vitest.integration.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    include: ['src/**/*.integration.test.ts'],
    environment: 'node',
    experimentalVmThreads: false,
    // Disable Vite module runner for integration tests — use native Node.js imports
    // This is production-like: the test object is the same module the runtime will load
    viteModuleRunner: false,   // experimental in Vitest 4.1
    pool: 'forks',             // Recommended with viteModuleRunner:false for isolation
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      include: ['src/**/*.ts'],
      exclude: ['src/**/*.test.ts', 'src/**/*.spec.ts'],
    },
  },
});

// With viteModuleRunner:false, vi.mock() path aliases are not resolved via Vite
// Use jest-compatible module name mapping or absolute imports in integration tests:
import { createUserHandler } from '../../src/handlers/createUser.js'; // .js extension required
```

**Pyramid significance:** The Vite module sandbox adds startup overhead and resolves modules differently from Node.js's native `require`/`import`. For integration test cases that must test the same code path the production runtime uses, `viteModuleRunner: false` closes the gap between test environment and production environment — a key pyramid principle. The trade-off: `vi.mock()` path alias resolution is less reliable without the Vite layer; use explicit relative paths or configure `moduleNameMapper` equivalents.

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4-1 — experimental viteModuleRunner option]

---

### 8. Vitest 4.0 `toMatchScreenshot()` — Visual Regression at Component Test Level  [official]

Vitest 4.0 stabilises Browser Mode and introduces `toMatchScreenshot()` as a first-class visual regression assertion. Visual regression test cases now live in the Browser Mode integration layer — between unit test cases and full Playwright e2e test cases — rather than exclusively in expensive e2e suites.

```typescript
// vitest.browser.config.ts — separate Browser Mode project
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    include: ['src/**/*.visual.test.tsx'],
    browser: {
      enabled: true,
      provider: 'playwright',
      name: 'chromium',
      headless: true,
      screenshotFailures: true,
    },
  },
});

// src/components/PriceTag/PriceTag.visual.test.tsx
import { render } from 'vitest-browser-react';
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { PriceTag } from './PriceTag';

describe('PriceTag visual regression', () => {
  it('renders a standard price without discount', async () => {
    const { getByTestId } = render(<PriceTag price={29.99} currency="USD" />);
    const element = getByTestId('price-tag');

    // Captures a screenshot and diffs against baseline on subsequent runs
    await expect(element).toMatchScreenshot();
  });

  it('renders a strikethrough price with discount badge', async () => {
    const { getByTestId } = render(
      <PriceTag price={29.99} originalPrice={49.99} currency="USD" discountLabel="-40%" />
    );
    // Separate baseline per variant — each gets its own snapshot file
    await expect(getByTestId('price-tag')).toMatchScreenshot();
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** Visual regression test cases traditionally sat at the e2e level (Playwright `toMatchScreenshot`, Percy, Chromatic), making them expensive and slow. Vitest 4.0 Browser Mode visual regression runs against a mounted component without a full page load, cutting test execution time by ~80% and moving a class of e2e-only test cases down to the integration/component level — a structural improvement in the pyramid shape.

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4 — toMatchScreenshot and Browser Mode stable]

### 9. Node.js 26 `--test-randomize` + Reproducible Seeds for Order-Dependency Detection  [official]

Node.js 26.1.0 adds `--test-randomize` and `--test-random-seed=N` to the built-in `node:test` runner, providing framework-independent order-dependency detection. This matters at the integration test level, where shared database state or in-process singletons create the most common hidden dependencies.

```typescript
// package.json — CI script to detect order-dependent integration tests
// "test:integration:randomize": "node --test --test-randomize --test-random-seed=$RANDOM src/**/*.integration.test.ts"

// test/integration/order-service.integration.test.ts
import { describe, it, before, after } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { OrderService } from '../../src/services/OrderService.js';
import { resetDatabase, seedDatabase } from '../helpers/db.js';

describe('OrderService integration', () => {
  before(async () => {
    await resetDatabase();
    await seedDatabase({ users: 3, products: 10 });
  });

  after(async () => {
    await resetDatabase();
  });

  it('creates an order for a known product', async () => {
    const svc = new OrderService();
    const order = await svc.create({ userId: 'u-1', productId: 'p-1', qty: 2 });
    assert.equal(order.status, 'pending');
    assert.equal(order.qty, 2);
  });

  it('rejects an order for an out-of-stock product', async () => {
    const svc = new OrderService();
    // If this test case runs first (in random mode), the product seed must guarantee
    // at least one out-of-stock item — do not depend on a previous test case depleting stock
    await assert.rejects(
      svc.create({ userId: 'u-1', productId: 'p-oos', qty: 1 }),
      { message: /out of stock/ }
    );
  });
});

// CI invocation — print seed for reproduction on failure:
// node --test --test-randomize 2>&1 | tee test-output.txt
// # "Randomized test order seed: 1684321456" → replay with --test-random-seed=1684321456
```

**Pyramid significance:** Hidden test-case order dependencies are the most prevalent integration test defect in TypeScript codebases with shared infrastructure (PostgreSQL, Redis, in-process event buses). Running order randomisation weekly in CI surfaces these defects before they cause non-reproducible pipeline failures. Works with `describe`/`it` style; does not randomise sequentially-awaited subtests inside a `test()` function.

[official: nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/test.html — --test-randomize v26.1.0]

### 10. Node.js 26 `expectFailure` as Structured Quarantine (Not a Permanent Fix)  [official]

`node:test`'s `expectFailure` option (v24.14.0, stable in v25.5.0) marks a test case as expected to fail — inverting pass/fail reporting. It provides a structured quarantine mechanism superior to `test.skip()` because it still runs the test case and fails the suite if the defect is unexpectedly fixed without the `expectFailure` marker being removed.

```typescript
// integration test with known defect under investigation — uses node:test built-in
import { describe, it } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { BillingService } from '../../src/services/BillingService.js';

describe('BillingService integration', () => {
  it('generates a correct prorated invoice', async () => {
    const svc = new BillingService();
    const invoice = await svc.generateProrated({ userId: 'u-1', from: '2026-04-15' });
    assert.equal(invoice.total, 14.52); // correct expected value
  });

  // Defect QA-2847: prorated calculation off by $0.01 on leap-year months
  // Tracked: github.com/org/repo/issues/2847
  // Remove expectFailure once QA-2847 is resolved
  it('generates a correct prorated invoice for Feb in leap year', {
    expectFailure: {
      label: 'QA-2847: leap-year proration rounding defect',
      match: /Expected 13\.44 to equal 13\.45/,
    },
  }, async () => {
    const svc = new BillingService();
    const invoice = await svc.generateProrated({
      userId: 'u-1',
      from: '2028-02-15', // 2028 is a leap year
    });
    assert.strictEqual(invoice.total, 13.45);
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** `test.skip()` silently removes a test case from execution; `expectFailure` keeps it in the pipeline and reports a defect if the underlying code is accidentally fixed (the marker would need removal). This is the correct quarantine pattern at the integration level: keep the test case running, track the defect, and ensure the marker is removed when the defect is resolved. Anti-pattern: using `expectFailure` indefinitely as a permanent false-green accumulates technical debt.

[official: nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/test.html — expectFailure option, v25.5.0]

### 11. Vitest 4.1 `vi.defineHelper()` for Cleaner Custom Assertion Stack Traces  [official]

`vi.defineHelper()` wraps a custom assertion utility so that failure stack traces point to the test file call site rather than inside the utility function. Before this API, every custom `expectXxx(value)` helper appeared as the deepest frame in error output, obscuring which test case invoked it.

```typescript
// test/helpers/assertUser.ts — custom assertion utility
import { expect, vi } from 'vitest';

// Without vi.defineHelper — stack points inside assertUser.ts (unhelpful)
// export function assertUser(user: unknown, expected: Partial<User>) {
//   expect(user).toMatchObject(expected);
// }

// With vi.defineHelper — stack points to the test case call site
export const assertUser = vi.defineHelper(
  function assertUser(user: unknown, expected: Partial<{ id: string; email: string; role: string }>) {
    expect(user).toMatchObject({
      id: expect.any(String),
      ...expected,
    });
  }
);

// test/integration/auth.integration.test.ts
import { describe, it } from 'vitest';
import { assertUser } from '../helpers/assertUser';
import { AuthService } from '../../src/services/AuthService';

describe('AuthService integration', () => {
  it('returns a full user object after successful login', async () => {
    const svc = new AuthService();
    const user = await svc.login('alice@example.com', 'password123');
    // On failure, stack trace points here (line X in auth.integration.test.ts)
    // not inside assertUser.ts — immediately locating the defect
    assertUser(user, { email: 'alice@example.com', role: 'admin' });
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** Custom assertion utilities are the dominant pattern for reducing duplication in integration test suites. Before `vi.defineHelper()`, the stack-trace misdirection caused teams to abandon custom helpers and inline assertions directly — increasing duplication. This API removes that friction point and encourages the correct test-design pattern: assert observable outputs at the right abstraction level.

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4-1 — vi.defineHelper()]

### 12. Vitest 4.0 `expect.schemaMatching()` with Zod for Integration-Level Contract Validation  [official]

`expect.schemaMatching(schema)` accepts any Zod (or Valibot) schema and validates the actual value against it as an asymmetric matcher. At the integration test level this provides compile-time schema coupling between the test case and the API contract — a defect in the response shape fails the assertion with a Zod parse error, not a property-access TypeError.

```typescript
// test/integration/products-api.integration.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { z } from 'zod';
import { fetchProducts, createProduct } from '../../src/api/products';

// Centrally defined schema — shared with production validation
const ProductSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().uuid(),
  name: z.string().min(1),
  price: z.number().positive(),
  inStock: z.boolean(),
  createdAt: z.string().datetime(),
});

const ProductListResponseSchema = z.object({
  items: z.array(ProductSchema),
  total: z.number().int().nonneg(),
  page: z.number().int().positive(),
});

describe('Products API integration', () => {
  it('returns a valid product list response', async () => {
    const response = await fetchProducts({ page: 1, limit: 10 });

    // Validates the entire response structure against the Zod schema
    expect(response).toEqual(expect.schemaMatching(ProductListResponseSchema));
  });

  it('returns a single valid product after creation', async () => {
    const created = await createProduct({ name: 'Test Widget', price: 9.99 });
    expect(created).toEqual(expect.schemaMatching(ProductSchema));
  });
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** `expect.schemaMatching` closes the most common integration test gap in TypeScript projects: the divergence between the Zod schema used in production validation and the hand-maintained `expect.objectContaining({...})` assertions in test files. When the production schema changes, `expect.schemaMatching` automatically fails affected integration test cases — no manual test maintenance required.

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4 — expect.schemaMatching, Zod/Valibot support]

### 13. Jest 30 `jest.SpyInstance` Removal — Migrate to `jest.Spied<typeof fn>`  [official]

Jest 30 removes the `jest.SpyInstance` TypeScript type. The replacement is `jest.Spied<typeof originalFunction>` for method spies and `jest.MockedFunction<typeof fn>` for mocked functions. This is a purely compile-time breakage — runtime behaviour is unchanged — but it silently fails TypeScript compilation after upgrading.

```typescript
// BROKEN in Jest 30 — jest.SpyInstance removed
// import { jest } from '@jest/globals';
// let spy: jest.SpyInstance;
// spy = jest.spyOn(console, 'error');
// spy.mockImplementation(() => {});

// CORRECT in Jest 30:
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import { NotificationService } from '../../src/services/NotificationService';
import { EmailSender } from '../../src/infra/EmailSender';

describe('NotificationService', () => {
  let sendEmailSpy: jest.Spied<typeof EmailSender.prototype.send>;

  beforeEach(() => {
    sendEmailSpy = jest.spyOn(EmailSender.prototype, 'send')
      .mockResolvedValue({ messageId: 'msg-123' });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    sendEmailSpy.mockRestore();
  });

  it('sends a welcome email after user registration', async () => {
    const svc = new NotificationService(new EmailSender());
    await svc.onUserRegistered({ userId: 'u-1', email: 'new@example.com' });
    expect(sendEmailSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ to: 'new@example.com', template: 'welcome' })
    );
  });
});
```

**Migration automation:** The eslint-plugin-jest autofixer handles the alias removals (`toBeCalled → toHaveBeenCalled`) but does not fix `SpyInstance`. Add a codemod to `package.json` pre-upgrade: `npx jscodeshift -t @jest/codemods/transforms/jest-spied.js 'src/**/*.test.ts'`.

[official: jestjs.io/docs/upgrading-to-jest30 — removed TypeScript types: SpyInstance]

### 14. Playwright v1.60 `tracing.startHar()` at the Integration Level  [official]

`tracing.startHar()` and `tracing.stopHar()` expose HAR recording as a first-class Playwright API (v1.60), independent of the full `tracing.start()` lifecycle. HAR files captured during integration API test cases can be replayed as mock responses in unit or component test cases, bridging the pyramid levels without requiring a running backend.

```typescript
// playwright.api.config.ts — API integration project
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
export default defineConfig({
  use: { baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000' },
  projects: [{ name: 'api-integration', testMatch: '**/*.api.test.ts' }],
});

// tests/api/products.api.test.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'node:path';
import fs from 'node:fs';

test.describe('Products API — HAR capture for downstream mocking', () => {
  test('capture GET /products response into HAR fixture', async ({ request }, testInfo) => {
    const harPath = path.join('test/fixtures', 'products-list.har');
    const tracing = testInfo.project; // access project context

    // Use APIRequestContext directly — no browser needed
    // First: capture a real API response as a HAR fixture
    await request.storageState(); // ensure auth state is fresh

    const response = await request.get('/api/products?page=1&limit=10');
    expect(response.ok()).toBeTruthy();

    const body = await response.json();
    expect(body.items).toHaveLength(10);

    // Write HAR manually for route mocking in component tests
    // Note: page-level HAR via tracing.startHar() captures browser network traffic
    // For API integration, response bodies are asserted directly above
  });
});

// tests/components/ProductList.browser.test.tsx — uses captured HAR as route mock
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/experimental-ct-react';
import { ProductList } from '../../src/components/ProductList';

test('renders products from HAR fixture', async ({ page, mount }) => {
  // Route all /api/products calls to the previously captured HAR
  await page.routeFromHAR('test/fixtures/products-list.har', {
    url: '**/api/products**',
    update: false, // use existing HAR; set true to refresh
  });
  const component = await mount(<ProductList />);
  await expect(component.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(10);
});
```

**Pyramid significance:** HAR-based mocking in component test cases decouples the component test level from a running backend while using real production responses (not hand-crafted stubs). The integration test case generates the fixture; the component test case consumes it. This is a structured two-level pyramid technique: integration validates the contract; component validates the rendering logic against a known-good response.

[official: playwright.dev/docs/release-notes — v1.60 tracing.startHar()/stopHar()]

### 15. Vitest 4.1 `coverage.changed` — Per-PR Coverage Delta Without Full Suite Overhead  [official]

`coverage.changed: true` restricts coverage collection to files touched in the current git diff, dramatically reducing coverage overhead for large monorepos where running full-suite coverage is too slow for per-PR CI gates.

```typescript
// vitest.coverage.config.ts — used in PR CI only
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
import { execSync } from 'node:child_process';

// Determine changed files relative to base branch
const changedFiles = execSync('git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD')
  .toString()
  .split('\n')
  .filter(f => f.endsWith('.ts') && !f.endsWith('.test.ts'));

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      enabled: true,
      // Only collect coverage for changed source files
      include: changedFiles.length ? changedFiles : ['src/**/*.ts'],
      exclude: ['src/**/*.test.ts', 'src/**/*.spec.ts'],
      thresholds: {
        lines: 80,
        branches: 75,
        functions: 80,
        statements: 80,
        // Fail CI if any changed file falls below threshold
        perFile: true,
      },
      reporter: ['text', 'json-summary', 'html'],
    },
  },
});

// GitHub Actions workflow step:
// - name: Run coverage for changed files
//   run: npx vitest run --config vitest.coverage.config.ts
// - name: Report coverage delta
//   uses: davelosert/vitest-coverage-report-action@v2
//   with:
//     json-summary-path: coverage/coverage-summary.json
```

**Pyramid significance:** Full-suite coverage in large TypeScript codebases can take 10-20 minutes. `coverage.changed` gates each PR on the coverage of files the PR author actually touched, keeping the feedback loop fast while enforcing meaningful thresholds. The pattern pairs with per-file `thresholds.perFile: true` to prevent individual files from falling below the minimum while the aggregate stays green.

[official: vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4-1 — coverage.changed option]
