### Pattern 311 — Playwright `mergeExpects()` for Composable Custom Matcher Libraries [official]

**Description.** Large TypeScript projects accumulate domain-specific assertion helpers (e.g., `toBeValidOrder()`, `toMatchApiContract()`, `toHaveAccessibleLabel()`). Playwright's `mergeExpects()` utility composes multiple `expect.extend()` sets into a single typed `expect` object, keeping matcher files modular and independently testable. Each domain module exports its own `expect` handle; the test file imports the merged handle that carries all types.

```typescript
// tests/matchers/order-matchers.ts
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

export const orderExpect = expect.extend({
  async toBeValidOrder(locator: import('@playwright/test').Locator) {
    const orderId = await locator.getByTestId('order-id').textContent();
    const status = await locator.getByTestId('order-status').textContent();
    const pass =
      orderId !== null &&
      /^ORD-\d{6}$/.test(orderId.trim()) &&
      ['pending', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered'].includes(
        status?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '',
      );
    return {
      pass,
      message: () =>
        `expected order card to be valid (id="${orderId}", status="${status}")`,
    };
  },
});

// tests/matchers/a11y-matchers.ts
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

export const a11yExpect = expect.extend({
  async toHaveNoAria(locator: import('@playwright/test').Locator) {
    const role = await locator.getAttribute('role');
    const pass = role === null;
    return {
      pass,
      message: () => `expected element to have no explicit ARIA role`,
    };
  },
});

// tests/fixtures/merged-expect.ts
import { mergeExpects } from '@playwright/test';
import { orderExpect } from '../matchers/order-matchers';
import { a11yExpect } from '../matchers/a11y-matchers';

// Produces a single expect with union of all matcher types
export const expect = mergeExpects(orderExpect, a11yExpect);

// tests/order-dashboard.e2e.ts
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import { expect } from '../fixtures/merged-expect';

test('order card renders correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/orders/ORD-000042');
  const card = page.getByTestId('order-card');
  await expect(card).toBeValidOrder();
  await expect(card.getByRole('heading')).toHaveNoAria();
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `mergeExpects()` requires TypeScript to resolve the union of matcher type declarations at compile time; with more than ~8 separate `expect.extend()` modules, type inference can slow down `tsc --noEmit`. Benchmark with `--extendedDiagnostics` if CI type-check times degrade. Do not re-export the merged `expect` from a barrel `index.ts` that also re-exports Playwright's base `expect` — the name collision causes the wrong overload to be selected. Keep each merged `expect` in its own fixture file.

---

### Pattern 312 — Playwright `test.step()` with Per-Step Timeout via `TestStepInfo` [official]

**Description.** Playwright v1.51+ allows individual steps inside a `test.step()` call to carry their own timeout, independent of the overall test timeout. The step callback now receives a `TestStepInfo` argument that exposes `step.setTimeout()`. This pattern is essential for e2e tests that mix fast UI interactions with slow external API calls: the slow steps get a generous timeout while the fast steps use a tight one, catching regressions in interaction speed.

```typescript
// tests/checkout.e2e.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('complete checkout journey', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/cart');

  // Fast UI interaction — tight 2 s timeout surfaces regressions immediately
  await test.step('fill shipping form', async (step) => {
    step.setTimeout(2_000);
    await page.getByLabel('Full name').fill('Jane Doe');
    await page.getByLabel('Address').fill('123 Main St');
    await page.getByLabel('City').fill('Springfield');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue to payment' }).click();
  });

  // Payment gateway integration — allow up to 15 s for external round-trip
  await test.step('submit payment', async (step) => {
    step.setTimeout(15_000);
    await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4242424242424242');
    await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/28');
    await page.getByLabel('CVC').fill('123');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay now' }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Order confirmed' }))
      .toBeVisible();
  });

  // Post-confirmation step — tight again once we are back on our own UI
  await test.step('verify confirmation page', async (step) => {
    step.setTimeout(3_000);
    await expect(page.getByTestId('order-id')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('receipt-email')).toContainText('jane@');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Per-step timeouts do not override the parent test timeout — if the sum of all per-step timeouts exceeds `testOptions.timeout`, the test will still fail at the outer limit. Use per-step timeouts as a diagnostic tool to pinpoint which step is slow, not as a way to extend the overall test budget. When a step timeout fires, Playwright reports the specific step name in the failure message, which makes triage far faster than a generic "test exceeded timeout" error.

---

### Pattern 313 — Vitest `test.aroundEach()` for Transaction-Wrapped Integration Tests [official]

**Description.** Vitest 4.1 introduced `test.aroundEach()` and `test.aroundAll()` hooks that wrap tests in a context — analogous to a try/finally or a database transaction. The pattern replaces paired `beforeEach`/`afterEach` for integration tests that need atomic rollback: begin a transaction in the "before" phase, yield to the test, then rollback unconditionally in the "after" phase regardless of test outcome.

```typescript
// tests/integration/user-repository.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { db } from '../../src/db/client';

describe('UserRepository', () => {
  // aroundEach wraps every test in a rolled-back transaction
  test.aroundEach(async (run) => {
    // Start a transaction and expose it through a pg savepoint
    await db.query('BEGIN');
    await db.query('SAVEPOINT test_savepoint');

    try {
      await run(); // execute the test body
    } finally {
      // Always roll back — test passes or fails
      await db.query('ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT test_savepoint');
      await db.query('ROLLBACK');
    }
  });

  test('creates a user with hashed password', async () => {
    const result = await db.query(
      `INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash)
       VALUES ($1, $2) RETURNING id`,
      ['alice@example.com', 'hashed-pw'],
    );
    expect(result.rows[0].id).toBeTypeOf('number');

    // Verify the row exists within this transaction
    const check = await db.query(
      'SELECT email FROM users WHERE id = $1',
      [result.rows[0].id],
    );
    expect(check.rows[0].email).toBe('alice@example.com');
    // After the test, aroundEach rolls back — no cleanup needed
  });

  test('rejects duplicate email', async () => {
    await db.query(
      `INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash) VALUES ($1, $2)`,
      ['bob@example.com', 'pw1'],
    );
    await expect(
      db.query(
        `INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash) VALUES ($1, $2)`,
        ['bob@example.com', 'pw2'],
      ),
    ).rejects.toThrow(/duplicate key/);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `aroundEach()` couples test isolation to the database transaction model. If your schema uses `ON COMMIT` triggers or deferred constraints, the trigger/constraint fires only at `COMMIT` time, meaning it will never fire inside the wrapped transaction, giving false-green test results for constraint checks. Use `aroundEach()` only when you have verified that all relevant constraints are `NOT DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE`. For deferred-constraint scenarios, use `beforeEach`/`afterEach` with truncation instead.

---

### Pattern 314 — Vitest Test Tags with `--reporter=verbose` Filtering for Pyramid-Level CI Jobs [official]

**Description.** Vitest 4.0+ `tags` option on test or `describe` blocks allows labelling tests by pyramid level (`:unit`, `:integration`, `:e2e`) and by concern (`:slow`, `:db`, `:network`). The `--tags-filter` CLI flag runs only the matching subset, enabling fast unit-only CI jobs on every push and full-pyramid jobs on main-branch merges — without separate config files.

```typescript
// src/pricing/discount.test.ts  — tagged unit test
import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { applyDiscount } from './discount';

describe('applyDiscount', { tags: [':unit'] }, () => {
  test('applies percentage discount correctly', () => {
    expect(applyDiscount(100, { type: 'percent', value: 20 })).toBe(80);
  });

  test('caps discount at item price', () => {
    expect(applyDiscount(50, { type: 'fixed', value: 100 })).toBe(0);
  });
});

// tests/integration/discount-api.test.ts — tagged integration test
import { describe, test, expect, beforeAll, afterAll } from 'vitest';
import { createServer } from '../../src/server';
import supertest from 'supertest';

describe('POST /discounts/apply', { tags: [':integration', ':db'] }, () => {
  let server: ReturnType<typeof createServer>;

  beforeAll(() => { server = createServer(); });
  afterAll(() => server.close());

  test('applies discount for authenticated user', async () => {
    const res = await supertest(server)
      .post('/discounts/apply')
      .set('Authorization', 'Bearer test-token')
      .send({ itemId: 'PROD-001', discountCode: 'SAVE20' });

    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.body.finalPrice).toBeTypeOf('number');
  });
});

// vitest.config.ts — no tags-filter here; tags are specified at CLI time
// CI push job: vitest run --tags-filter=:unit
// CI PR job:   vitest run --tags-filter=:unit,:integration
// CI nightly:  vitest run  (no filter — all tags including :e2e)
```

**Tradeoff.** Tags are a naming convention, not a runtime enforcement mechanism — nothing prevents a test tagged `:unit` from making real network calls. Teams must pair tag governance with linting (a custom ESLint rule that disallows `node:net`/`fetch` imports in files that only contain `:unit`-tagged suites). Also, `--tags-filter` is additive OR logic by default: `--tags-filter=:unit,:integration` runs tests tagged with either tag, not both. Use `--tags-filter=:unit AND :fast` syntax (with the `AND` keyword) for intersection filtering.

---

### Pattern 315 — Playwright `locator.and()` for Compound Role + Text Queries [official]

**Description.** `locator.and(otherLocator)` narrows a locator to elements that match *both* conditions simultaneously, replacing fragile chained `.filter()` calls that may match intermediate DOM nodes. The primary use case is combining role-based queries (accessibility-first) with text or attribute conditions without resorting to CSS selectors.

```typescript
// tests/product-list.e2e.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('sale badge is visible on discounted products', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');

  // Compound: element must be a listitem AND contain the sale price text
  const saleItem = page
    .getByRole('listitem')
    .and(page.getByText(/was \$\d+\.\d{2}/));

  // Assert the compound locator matches at least one result
  await expect(saleItem.first()).toBeVisible();

  // Further narrow: the sale item's discount badge
  const badge = saleItem
    .first()
    .getByRole('img', { name: /sale|discount/i })
    .and(page.locator('[data-testid="discount-badge"]'));

  await expect(badge).toBeVisible();
  await expect(badge).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', /\d+% off/);
});

test('add-to-cart button is enabled only when in stock', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products/PROD-001');

  // Role + attribute compound: button that is both "Add to cart" and not disabled
  const addButton = page
    .getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' })
    .and(page.locator(':not([disabled])'));

  await expect(addButton).toBeVisible();
  await addButton.click();

  const cartCount = page.getByRole('status', { name: /cart/i });
  await expect(cartCount).toContainText('1');
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `locator.and()` performs a DOM intersection at query time, meaning both constituent locators are evaluated independently and the result is the intersection. This is slightly more expensive than a single CSS selector for large DOMs. More importantly, `locator.and()` is strict by default: if the intersection matches zero elements, Playwright throws immediately rather than retrying with the outer locator. Design compound locators so that when the feature is working correctly, the intersection always yields exactly one element — use `.first()` or `.nth()` only when the page legitimately shows multiples.

---

### Pattern 316 — Vitest `coverage.htmlDir` + `coverage.changed` for Per-PR Coverage Reports [official]

**Description.** Vitest 4.1 added `coverage.htmlDir` to control where the HTML coverage report is written (separate from the standard output directory), enabling CI to upload it as a named artefact per branch. Combined with `coverage.changed` (which limits instrumentation to files touched by the current git diff), this produces fast, focused coverage feedback scoped to the PR's changes rather than the entire codebase.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      enabled: true,
      // Only instrument files that changed relative to the base branch
      changed: process.env.CI ? 'origin/main' : undefined,

      // Write HTML report to a fixed path so CI can upload it as an artifact
      htmlDir: 'coverage-html',

      // Thresholds apply to the changed-files subset when `changed` is set
      thresholds: {
        lines: 80,
        branches: 75,
        functions: 80,
        statements: 80,
      },

      // Exclude test files, generated code, and config from coverage
      exclude: [
        '**/*.test.ts',
        '**/*.spec.ts',
        '**/node_modules/**',
        '**/dist/**',
        'vitest.config.ts',
        'src/generated/**',
      ],
    },
  },
});

// .github/workflows/pr.yml (relevant excerpt)
// - name: Run tests with coverage
//   run: vitest run --coverage
//   env:
//     CI: true
// - name: Upload HTML coverage report
//   uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
//   with:
//     name: coverage-report-${{ github.sha }}
//     path: coverage-html/
//     retention-days: 7
```

**Tradeoff.** `coverage.changed` compares against the git ref provided (e.g., `origin/main`). If the CI runner does a shallow clone (`fetch-depth: 1`), the ref may not be available, causing Vitest to fall back to full instrumentation silently. Set `fetch-depth: 0` in the CI checkout step when using `coverage.changed`. Also, per-PR coverage numbers are only meaningful when the changed files have meaningful test coverage — a PR that adds only test files will show 100% trivially. Enforce that coverage thresholds apply to the *source* files changed, not the test files themselves, using the `exclude` pattern.

---

### Pattern 317 — Playwright HAR Replay for Deterministic Integration-Level API Testing [official]

**Description.** Playwright's HAR (HTTP Archive) recording and replay capability enables a class of tests that sits between pure integration (MSW mocks) and live e2e (real network): record a real API interaction once, then replay the HAR deterministically in CI. The recorded file is committed to version control and becomes a regression anchor — if the API contract changes, the replay fails and prompts a deliberate re-record.

```typescript
// tests/fixtures/har-fixtures.ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

type HarFixtures = {
  withHar: (harName: string) => Promise<void>;
};

export const test = base.extend<HarFixtures>({
  withHar: async ({ page }, use) => {
    const withHar = async (harName: string) => {
      const harPath = path.join(__dirname, '../hars', `${harName}.har`);
      await page.routeFromHAR(harPath, {
        // Strict mode: fail the test if a request is not in the HAR
        notFound: 'abort',
        // Match on URL + method; ignore query-string order differences
        url: '**',
        update: process.env.UPDATE_HAR === 'true',
      });
    };
    await use(withHar);
  },
});

// tests/product-detail.test.ts
import { test, expect } from './fixtures/har-fixtures';

test('product detail page renders from HAR', async ({ page, withHar }) => {
  // In CI: replays from the committed HAR file
  // With UPDATE_HAR=true: records a fresh HAR from the live API
  await withHar('product-PROD-001');
  await page.goto('/products/PROD-001');

  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 }))
    .toContainText('Wireless Headphones');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('price')).toContainText('$79.99');
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }))
    .toBeEnabled();
});

// To refresh the HAR: UPDATE_HAR=true npx playwright test product-detail
```

**Tradeoff.** HAR files grow large for API-heavy pages (JSON payloads, images, fonts). Commit only the API calls you care about by setting `url` to match only the API origin (e.g., `https://api.example.com/**`) rather than `**`. The HAR approach is ideal for external third-party APIs where you cannot run a local server, but it does not test server-side logic — it only tests how the frontend consumes the responses. Rotate HAR files when the API schema changes deliberately; stale HARs mask schema drift from the e2e suite.

---

### Pattern 318 — Playwright `--only-changed` for PR-Scoped E2E Execution [official]

**Description.** Playwright v1.52+ `--only-changed` flag compares the current git diff against a base ref and runs only the test files whose source or imported modules changed. Combined with Playwright's `testProject` dependencies, this enables a CI pipeline that skips unrelated e2e suites entirely, reducing PR feedback time from 20+ minutes to under 5 minutes for typical PRs.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './tests',

  // Projects allow --only-changed to scope by project too
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
      testMatch: '**/*.e2e.ts',
    },
    {
      name: 'mobile',
      use: { ...devices['Pixel 7'] },
      // Mobile project only runs checkout and product tests
      testMatch: '**/checkout/**/*.e2e.ts',
      dependencies: ['chromium'],
    },
    {
      name: 'api-smoke',
      testMatch: '**/api/**/*.e2e.ts',
    },
  ],
});

// CI usage (GitHub Actions excerpt):
// - name: Run only changed e2e tests
//   run: |
//     npx playwright test \
//       --only-changed=origin/main \
//       --project=chromium \
//       --reporter=github
//
// Full suite still runs on merge to main:
// - name: Full e2e suite (post-merge)
//   if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
//   run: npx playwright test --project=chromium --project=mobile
```

**Tradeoff.** `--only-changed` uses Playwright's static module graph analysis to find affected tests. It cannot detect runtime dynamic imports (`import(variable)`) or tests whose behaviour changes due to shared fixture code that is not explicitly imported — these must be tracked separately. The safest strategy: use `--only-changed` on PR jobs to accelerate feedback; always run the full suite on merge to main to catch fixture or configuration regressions that `--only-changed` would skip.

---

### Pattern 319 — Vitest Agent Reporter for AI-Assisted Development Workflows [official]

**Description.** Vitest 4.1's `agent` reporter outputs only failing tests with minimal decoration — no progress bars, no passing test names, no colour codes. This mode is optimised for AI coding agent workflows (Claude Code, Copilot Workspace) where the model reads test output to determine which fixes to apply. Suppressing passing-test noise cuts token usage by 60–80% in typical suites and makes the failure signal cleaner for model parsing.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts — agent reporter enabled via env var
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    reporters: process.env.AGENT_MODE
      ? ['agent']                       // minimal: only failures
      : ['verbose', 'github-actions'],  // full output for humans + CI annotations

    // Pair with detectAsyncLeaks so the agent sees async resource leaks too
    detectAsyncLeaks: true,

    // Use coverage.changed so the agent only gets coverage for changed files
    coverage: {
      enabled: !!process.env.AGENT_MODE,
      changed: process.env.AGENT_MODE ? 'HEAD~1' : undefined,
      reporter: ['text'],   // text is token-efficient; skip html in agent mode
    },
  },
});

// Usage patterns:
//   Normal dev:     vitest run
//   CI:             vitest run (uses reporters array default)
//   AI agent loop:  AGENT_MODE=1 vitest run
//
// In the AI coding loop the agent reads only failure output:
// FAIL tests/pricing/discount.test.ts > applyDiscount > caps discount at item price
//   AssertionError: expected 5 to be 0
//   at discount.test.ts:14:30
```

**Tradeoff.** The `agent` reporter is token-efficient but it hides passing test counts, skipped tests, and timing information. Do not use it as the primary reporter in CI dashboards — humans reviewing CI logs lose the quick-glance green/red summary. A good compromise is enabling the `agent` reporter only when `AGENT_MODE` or a similar environment variable is set, and using `verbose` + `github-actions` reporters for all other contexts. Note that the reporter name is `agent`, not `minimal` — confusing the two causes Vitest to silently fall back to the default reporter.

---

### Pattern 320 — Playwright `browser.newContext()` with `storageState` Composition for Multi-Role E2E Tests [official]

**Description.** E2e tests for admin, manager, and customer flows each require a distinct authenticated session. Rather than logging in at the start of every test, Playwright's `storageState` serialises the browser's cookies and `localStorage` after a one-time login in a global setup file. Tests compose multiple named states to validate cross-role interactions (e.g., an admin publishes a product; a customer sees it immediately).

```typescript
// tests/global-setup.ts
import { chromium, FullConfig } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

async function globalSetup(config: FullConfig) {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();

  // Authenticate as admin
  const adminCtx = await browser.newContext();
  const adminPage = await adminCtx.newPage();
  await adminPage.goto(`${config.projects[0].use.baseURL}/login`);
  await adminPage.getByLabel('Email').fill('admin@example.com');
  await adminPage.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.ADMIN_PW!);
  await adminPage.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await adminPage.waitForURL('**/dashboard');
  await adminCtx.storageState({ path: path.join(__dirname, '../.auth/admin.json') });

  // Authenticate as customer
  const customerCtx = await browser.newContext();
  const customerPage = await customerCtx.newPage();
  await customerPage.goto(`${config.projects[0].use.baseURL}/login`);
  await customerPage.getByLabel('Email').fill('customer@example.com');
  await customerPage.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.CUSTOMER_PW!);
  await customerPage.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await customerPage.waitForURL('**/home');
  await customerCtx.storageState({ path: path.join(__dirname, '../.auth/customer.json') });

  await browser.close();
}

export default globalSetup;

// tests/cross-role-publish.e2e.ts
import { test, expect, Browser } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

test('admin publishes product; customer sees it immediately', async ({ browser }) => {
  // Admin context
  const adminCtx = await browser.newContext({
    storageState: path.join(__dirname, '../.auth/admin.json'),
  });
  const adminPage = await adminCtx.newPage();

  // Customer context (parallel, different session)
  const customerCtx = await browser.newContext({
    storageState: path.join(__dirname, '../.auth/customer.json'),
  });
  const customerPage = await customerCtx.newPage();

  // Admin publishes
  await adminPage.goto('/admin/products/new');
  await adminPage.getByLabel('Product name').fill('Test Product');
  await adminPage.getByRole('button', { name: 'Publish' }).click();
  await expect(adminPage.getByRole('alert')).toContainText('Published');

  // Customer sees it immediately in their session
  await customerPage.goto('/products');
  await customerPage.getByPlaceholder('Search products').fill('Test Product');
  await expect(customerPage.getByRole('listitem').filter({ hasText: 'Test Product' }))
    .toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });

  await adminCtx.close();
  await customerCtx.close();
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Storing auth state as committed `.json` files is a security risk if the tokens are long-lived and the repository is public. Use short-lived tokens or test-environment credentials, and add `.auth/` to `.gitignore` — store the files in a CI secret or generate them at runtime. The `storageState` pattern speeds up test suites by 40–60% for auth-heavy flows, but it creates a coupling between the global setup and every test that uses the state file; if the login page changes, all state files need regeneration.

---

### Pattern 321 — Vitest `vi.mockThrow()` / `vi.mockThrowOnce()` for Error-Path Unit Tests [official]

**Description.** Vitest 4.1 introduced `vi.mockThrow()` and `vi.mockThrowOnce()` as concise alternatives to the verbose `vi.fn().mockImplementation(() => { throw new Error(...) })` pattern. The new APIs reduce error-path unit test boilerplate and produce cleaner stack traces because the throw originates at the mock definition site, not inside an anonymous closure.

```typescript
// src/payment/charge.ts
export type ChargeResult = { transactionId: string; amount: number };
export type PaymentGateway = {
  charge(amount: number, token: string): Promise<ChargeResult>;
};
export async function processPayment(
  amount: number,
  token: string,
  gateway: PaymentGateway,
): Promise<ChargeResult> {
  try {
    return await gateway.charge(amount, token);
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof Error && err.message.includes('card_declined')) {
      throw Object.assign(new Error('Payment declined'), { code: 'DECLINED' });
    }
    throw err;
  }
}

// tests/payment/charge.unit.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import { processPayment, type PaymentGateway } from '../../src/payment/charge';

describe('processPayment error paths', () => {
  test('wraps card_declined gateway error', async () => {
    const gateway: PaymentGateway = {
      charge: vi.fn(),
    };

    // New API: mockThrowOnce — no anonymous closure needed
    vi.mocked(gateway.charge).mockThrowOnce(new Error('card_declined'));

    await expect(processPayment(100, 'tok_test', gateway))
      .rejects.toMatchObject({ message: 'Payment declined', code: 'DECLINED' });
  });

  test('re-throws unknown gateway errors unchanged', async () => {
    const gateway: PaymentGateway = { charge: vi.fn() };

    // mockThrow makes every call throw (not just once)
    vi.mocked(gateway.charge).mockThrow(new Error('network_timeout'));

    await expect(processPayment(100, 'tok_test', gateway))
      .rejects.toThrow('network_timeout');

    // Verify throw was called exactly once
    expect(gateway.charge).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  test('succeeds on happy path after error is cleared', async () => {
    const gateway: PaymentGateway = { charge: vi.fn() };
    vi.mocked(gateway.charge).mockThrowOnce(new Error('transient'));
    // Second call should resolve normally (mockThrowOnce fires only once)
    vi.mocked(gateway.charge).mockResolvedValueOnce({
      transactionId: 'txn_abc', amount: 100,
    });

    await expect(processPayment(100, 'tok_test', gateway))
      .rejects.toThrow('transient');
    await expect(processPayment(100, 'tok_test', gateway))
      .resolves.toMatchObject({ transactionId: 'txn_abc' });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `mockThrow()` and `mockThrowOnce()` accept a value, not a factory function — the error object is evaluated once at the call site and reused for all invocations in the `mockThrow()` case. If your test needs each invocation to throw a distinct error instance (e.g., to verify that different `instanceId` properties are set on separate errors), you still need `mockImplementation(() => { throw new SomeError(nextId++) })`. Also, `mockThrow()` does not distinguish between synchronous throws and rejected promises — for async mocks the thrown value is automatically wrapped in a `Promise.reject()`; do not mix `mockThrow()` with `mockResolvedValue()` on the same mock function as the precedence order can be surprising.

---

### Pattern 322 — Playwright `toHaveCSS()` with Pseudo-Element Targeting [official]

**Description.** Playwright v1.60 extended `toHaveCSS()` to accept an optional `pseudo` option for asserting CSS properties on `::before`, `::after`, and other CSS pseudo-elements. This fills a long-standing gap in visual regression testing: pseudo-element styles (decorative icons, clearfix tricks, focus rings rendered as `::before` overlays) were previously invisible to assertion APIs without resorting to JavaScript `getComputedStyle(el, '::before')` evaluation.

```typescript
// tests/button-styles.e2e.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('primary button renders correct focus ring via ::before', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/button');

  const button = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });
  await button.focus();

  // Assert the ::before pseudo-element carries the focus ring style
  await expect(button).toHaveCSS('opacity', '1', { pseudo: '::before' });
  await expect(button).toHaveCSS('border', /2px solid/, { pseudo: '::before' });
});

test('required field shows asterisk via ::after', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/forms/registration');

  const label = page.getByText('Email address').locator('..');
  // The ::after pseudo-element renders the required asterisk
  await expect(label).toHaveCSS('content', '"*"', { pseudo: '::after' });
  await expect(label).toHaveCSS('color', 'rgb(220, 38, 38)', { pseudo: '::after' });
});

test('skeleton loader uses ::after animation', async ({ page }) => {
  // Intercept the API to keep the skeleton visible
  await page.route('**/api/users', async (route) => {
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2_000));
    await route.fulfill({ json: [] });
  });

  await page.goto('/users');

  const skeleton = page.getByTestId('user-skeleton').first();
  await expect(skeleton).toHaveCSS('animation-name', 'shimmer', {
    pseudo: '::after',
  });
  await expect(skeleton).toHaveCSS('animation-duration', '1.5s', {
    pseudo: '::after',
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `toHaveCSS()` with `pseudo` reads the *computed* CSS value, not the authored value. Shorthand properties (e.g., `border`) may be returned as the longhand expansion (`border-top: 2px solid rgb(0,0,0)`), so use regex matchers rather than exact string matching when asserting shorthands. Also, Playwright evaluates pseudo-element styles via `window.getComputedStyle(el, '::before')`, which only returns styles that are applied at the time of evaluation — if a CSS animation has not yet started (e.g., the page has not received focus), the animated property may return its initial value.

---

### Pattern 323 — Playwright `getByRole()` with `description` Option for ARIA Description Assertions [official]

**Description.** Playwright v1.60 added a `description` option to `getByRole()` that matches elements by their accessible description (from `aria-describedby`, `aria-description`, or `title` attribute), in addition to the existing `name` option. This enables tests to select elements with specificity that mirrors the experience of assistive technology users, and to verify that ARIA descriptions are wired correctly without resorting to `getByTestId()`.

```typescript
// tests/form-accessibility.e2e.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('password field has accessible strength description', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/register');

  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('weak');

  // Locate by role + accessible description — verifies aria-describedby wiring
  const passwordField = page.getByRole('textbox', {
    name: 'Password',
    description: /must be at least 8 characters/,
  });

  await expect(passwordField).toBeVisible();
  await expect(passwordField).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
});

test('progress bar has contextual accessible description', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/upload');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start upload' }).click();

  // The progress bar's aria-describedby points to a status message element
  const bar = page.getByRole('progressbar', {
    name: 'Upload progress',
    description: /uploading \d+ of \d+ files/i,
  });

  await expect(bar).toBeVisible();
  await expect(bar).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', /^\d+$/);
});

test('icon button has description distinguishing it from sibling', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/notifications');

  // Two "Delete" buttons — distinguished by accessible description
  const deleteRead = page.getByRole('button', {
    name: 'Delete',
    description: 'Delete read notifications',
  });
  const deleteAll = page.getByRole('button', {
    name: 'Delete',
    description: 'Delete all notifications',
  });

  await expect(deleteRead).toBeVisible();
  await expect(deleteAll).toBeVisible();
  // No ambiguity — each button's description uniquely identifies it
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `description` option matches against the *accessible description* as computed by the accessibility tree, not the raw HTML attribute value. If `aria-describedby` points to an element whose text is hidden with `display: none`, the accessible description may be empty — the locator will not match and the test will timeout with a confusing error. Always verify ARIA descriptions with Playwright's inspector (`page.accessibility.snapshot()`) during test development to confirm the computed description matches your expectation. Do not use `description` as a substitute for stable test IDs in complex dynamic UIs — the accessible description may be generated from user content (e.g., a notification's subject line) that changes between test runs.

---

### Pattern 324 — Vitest `aroundAll()` for Shared Container Lifecycle in Integration Test Suites [official]

**Description.** `test.aroundAll()` (Vitest 4.1) wraps the entire `describe` block in a single context, making it the natural fit for expensive shared resources like Testcontainers database instances or network servers that are too costly to start per-test. The pattern replaces the `beforeAll`/`afterAll` pair while guaranteeing cleanup even when the `describe` suite throws during setup.

```typescript
// tests/integration/product-repository.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { PostgreSqlContainer } from '@testcontainers/postgresql';
import { drizzle } from 'drizzle-orm/node-postgres';
import { Pool } from 'pg';
import { products } from '../../src/db/schema';

describe('ProductRepository', () => {
  let pool: Pool;
  let db: ReturnType<typeof drizzle>;

  // aroundAll: start container → run all tests → stop container (always)
  test.aroundAll(async (run) => {
    const container = await new PostgreSqlContainer('postgres:16-alpine')
      .withDatabase('testdb')
      .start();

    pool = new Pool({ connectionString: container.getConnectionUri() });
    db = drizzle(pool);

    // Run migrations inline
    await pool.query(`
      CREATE TABLE products (
        id   SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
        name TEXT NOT NULL,
        price NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL
      )
    `);

    try {
      await run(); // all tests in this describe block
    } finally {
      await pool.end();
      await container.stop();
    }
  });

  test('inserts and retrieves a product', async () => {
    await db.insert(products).values({ name: 'Widget', price: '9.99' });
    const result = await db.select().from(products);
    expect(result).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(result[0].name).toBe('Widget');
  });

  test('price is stored with decimal precision', async () => {
    const result = await db.select().from(products).limit(1);
    expect(Number(result[0].price)).toBeCloseTo(9.99, 2);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Unlike `beforeAll`/`afterAll`, `aroundAll()` provides a guarantee that `finally` always runs even if `run()` throws. However, if multiple `aroundAll()` hooks are nested (outer `describe` + inner `describe`), both `finally` blocks run in reverse registration order. The outer container is still running when the inner `aroundAll` teardown fires — this is correct but can mask container port-collision issues on CI runners with tight port ranges. When using `aroundAll()` with Testcontainers, set `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true` in CI to prevent the Ryuk reaper from racing with Vitest's own cleanup.

---

### Pattern 325 — Playwright `page.route()` with `route.fallback()` for Selective Network Mocking [official]

**Description.** `route.fallback()` passes an intercepted request to the next registered handler or to the network if no subsequent handler matches. This enables layered mocking strategies: a base handler stubs the entire API; a per-test handler overrides a specific endpoint while everything else falls through to the base stub. Tests can selectively inject error states without rewriting the entire mock surface.

```typescript
// tests/fixtures/api-base.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

// Base fixture: stub all API calls to return empty/default responses
export const test = base.extend({
  page: async ({ page }, use) => {
    // Default stub: 200 OK with empty collections for all API routes
    await page.route('**/api/**', async (route) => {
      const url = new URL(route.request().url());
      const defaults: Record<string, unknown> = {
        '/api/products': { items: [], total: 0 },
        '/api/cart': { items: [], subtotal: 0 },
        '/api/user/me': { id: 'u1', name: 'Test User', email: 'test@example.com' },
      };
      const body = defaults[url.pathname];
      if (body !== undefined) {
        await route.fulfill({ json: body });
      } else {
        await route.fallback(); // pass to next handler or real network
      }
    });
    await use(page);
  },
});

// tests/cart-error.e2e.ts
import { test, expect } from './fixtures/api-base';

test('shows error toast when cart API fails', async ({ page }) => {
  // Per-test override: make the cart endpoint return 500
  // This route is registered AFTER the base fixture, so it runs first
  await page.route('**/api/cart', async (route) => {
    await route.fulfill({ status: 500, body: 'Internal Server Error' });
    // No fallback — intercept ends here for /api/cart specifically
  });

  await page.goto('/cart');
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText('Failed to load cart');

  // /api/user/me still uses the base stub — the test is isolated
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toContainText('Test User');
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Routes are evaluated in reverse registration order: the most recently registered handler runs first. This ordering is intuitive for override patterns but counter-intuitive for developers used to Express-style middleware where the first match wins. When using `route.fallback()` in base fixtures, document the registration order explicitly. Be aware that `page.route()` handlers registered in a fixture are scoped to the page lifetime; `browserContext.route()` handlers persist across navigations in the same context. Use `page.route()` for per-test overrides and `browserContext.route()` only for session-wide stubs.

---

### Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 50)

201. **Vitest `aroundEach()` does not catch errors thrown in synchronous `beforeEach` hooks registered in the same `describe` block — if a `beforeEach` hook throws before the test body runs, the `aroundEach` wrapper's `run()` call never completes, but the `finally` block in `aroundEach` still executes; this causes the `finally` teardown to run on an incompletely-set-up resource, potentially triggering a secondary error that masks the original `beforeEach` failure** [community] — WHY: `aroundEach()` wraps the test execution phase (the `run()` call), which includes the test body and `afterEach` hooks but does not include `beforeEach` hooks registered in parent or sibling scopes. The `beforeEach` error causes `run()` to resolve with a rejection, but the `aroundEach` `finally` block still fires regardless. If the `finally` block depends on resources that `beforeEach` was supposed to set up (e.g., a database connection opened in `beforeEach`), the `finally` block throws a secondary error. Fix: move resource acquisition into `aroundEach` itself rather than split across `beforeEach`/`aroundEach` pairs; use a single `aroundEach` that both sets up and tears down the shared resource within the same wrapper function.

202. **Playwright `locator.and()` throws a strict-mode error when the compound intersection matches zero elements due to a CSS specificity conflict — when the second locator uses a CSS selector that applies a style overriding the first locator's visibility state (e.g., the first locator is `getByRole('button')` and the second is `locator('.hidden-button')` which has `display:none`), Playwright considers the intersection empty and throws immediately without retrying, producing an error that names the second locator but not the first, making triage difficult** [community] — WHY: `locator.and()` computes a DOM intersection — both constituent locators must match the same underlying element. If one locator's condition is incompatible with the other (e.g., role-based visibility vs. CSS class that hides the element), the intersection is empty and strict-mode throws. Playwright's retry mechanism does not apply to `locator.and()` when the intersection is provably empty (both locators resolve but share no common elements). Fix: always verify that the compound locator's conditions are mutually compatible before committing to the test; use `locator.count()` with a timeout guard in test development to confirm the intersection yields results before asserting.

203. **Vitest `coverage.changed` silently falls back to full-suite instrumentation when run in a detached HEAD state (common in GitHub Actions `pull_request` events with `fetch-depth: 1`) — the fallback behaviour is not logged at the default verbosity level, so CI coverage numbers appear unexpectedly large (full-codebase coverage instead of per-PR delta), and coverage thresholds that were calibrated for the delta fail on the full codebase** [community] — WHY: `coverage.changed` calls `git diff <base-ref>` to determine which files changed. In a detached HEAD state with shallow clone (`fetch-depth: 1`), the base ref (`origin/main`) is not available in the local git history and the `git diff` command fails. Vitest catches the failure internally and falls back to instrumenting all files, but does not emit a warning unless `--reporter=verbose` is set. Fix: set `fetch-depth: 0` in the GitHub Actions checkout step when using `coverage.changed`; or add an explicit `git fetch origin main` step before running Vitest to ensure the base ref is available.

204. **Playwright `route.fallback()` and `route.fulfill()` called in the same handler produce a "route already handled" error only in Playwright v1.55+ — older versions silently ignored the double-handling; teams upgrading from v1.53 find that route handlers which worked before now throw runtime errors in CI because a code path that previously did nothing now triggers a fatal error** [community] — WHY: Prior to v1.55, calling both `route.fallback()` and `route.fulfill()` in the same handler function was tolerated — the second call was silently ignored. Playwright v1.55 tightened the route handling contract: each route must be handled exactly once (via `fulfill`, `abort`, `continue`, or `fallback`). A handler that calls `route.fulfill()` and then falls through to a `route.fallback()` call in a subsequent `else` branch, or vice versa, now throws. Fix: ensure every code path in a route handler calls exactly one terminal method (`fulfill`, `abort`, `continue`, or `fallback`), and add ESLint `no-fallthrough`-style analysis or an integration test assertion that verifies all expected routes are handled exactly once.

205. **Vitest `vi.mockThrow()` does not reset automatically between tests even when `vi.clearAllMocks()` or `restoreAllMocks()` is called in `afterEach` — a `vi.mockThrow()` configured in one test will continue throwing in subsequent tests in the same file if the mock reference is shared across tests via a module-level `vi.fn()` variable; `clearAllMocks()` resets call counts and implementations set via `mockImplementation()` but `mockThrow()` is treated as a "permanent" implementation modifier that survives `clearAllMocks()`** [community] — WHY: `vi.mockThrow()` internally calls `mockImplementation(() => { throw value })`, which sets the mock's implementation. `clearAllMocks()` clears call history (`.mock.calls`, `.mock.results`) and removes one-time implementations set with `mockImplementationOnce()`, but it does NOT clear the base implementation set by `mockImplementation()`. Since `mockThrow()` delegates to `mockImplementation()`, the throw persists. Fix: use `vi.resetAllMocks()` (which also resets the base implementation) instead of `vi.clearAllMocks()` in `afterEach` when using `mockThrow()`; or use `vi.mockThrowOnce()` instead of `vi.mockThrow()` for error paths that should apply to only one test invocation.
